hymns.title: Jesus Grant That Balm and Healing
hymns.music: 'Der Am Kreuz' Johann Balthasar König, 1738.  Setting: "Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book", 1931.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
Jesus, grant that balm and healing
In Thy holy wounds I find,
Every hour that I am feeling,
Pains of body and of mind.
Should some evil thought within
Tempt my treacherous heart to sin,
Show the peril, and from sinning
Keep me ere its first beginning.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
Should some lust or sharp temptation
Prove too strong for flesh and blood,
Let me think upon Thy Passion,
And the breach is soon made good.
Or should Satan press me hard,
Let me then be on my guard,
Saying, "Christ for me was wounded,"
That the tempter flee confounded.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
If the world my heart entices
On the broad and easy road
With its mirth and luring vices,
Let me think upon the load
Thou didst carry and endure
That I flee all thoughts impure,
Banishing each wild emotion,
Calm and blest in my devotion.

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
Every wound that pains or grieves me,
By Thy stripes, Lord, is made whole;
When I'm faint, Thy cross revives me,
Granting new life to my soul.
Yea, Thy comfort renders sweet
Every bitter cup I meet;
For Thy all atoning Passion
Has procured my soul's salvation.

parts.label: Verse 5
parts.lyrics:
O my God, my Rock and Tower,
Grant that in Thy death I trust,
Knowing death has lost his power
Since Thou trodd'st him in the dust.
Savior, let Thine agony
Ever help and comfort me;
When I die, be my Protection,
Light and Life and Resurrection.

parts.label: Verse 6
parts.lyrics:
Jesus, grant that balm and healing In Thy holy wounds I find,
Every hour that I am feeling, Pains of body and of mind.
And when I this world must leave, Grant that, Lord, to Thee I cleave,
In Thy wounds find consolation And obtain my soul's salvation

hymns.title: Jesus Is All the World To Me
hymns.words: Will L. Thompson, 1904.   Music 'Jesus Is All the World To Me' Will L. Thompson, 1904.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
Jesus is all the world to me,
My life, my joy, my all;
He is my strength from day to day,
Without Him I would fall.
When I am sad, to Him I go,
No other one can cheer me so;
When I am sad, He makes me glad,
He's my friend.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
Jesus is all the world to me,
my friend in trials sore;
I go to Him for blessings and
He gives them ov'r and o'er.
He sends the sunshine and the rain,
He sends the harvest's golden grain;
Sunshine and rain, harvest of grain,
He's my friend.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
Jesus is all the world to me,
and true to Him I'll be;
O how could I this friend deny,
when He's so true to me?
Following Him I know I'm right,
He watches o'er me day and night;
Following Him, by day and night,
He's my friend.

parts.label: Verse 4

hymns.title: Jesus Loves Me
hymns.music: 'untitled' by William B. Bradbury, 1862.  Setting: William B. Bradbury, 1866.
topics: Children (see also God's Children - the Faithful) [1,2]

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
Jesus loves me!
This I know,
For the Bible tells me so.
Little ones to Him belong;
They are weak, but He is strong.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
Jesus loves me! He who died
Heaven's gate to open wide; He will wash away my sin,
Let His little child come in.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
Jesus loves me! He will stay
Close beside me all the way; Thou hast bled and died for me, I will henceforth live for Thee.

parts.label: Refrain
parts.lyrics:
Yes, Jesus loves me!
Yes, Jesus loves me!
Yes, Jesus loves me!
The Bible tells me so.

hymns.title: Jesus Shall Reign
hymns.music: 'Duke Street' John Hatton, 1793.  Setting: "Christian Hymns", 1908.
topics: Children (see also God's Children - the Faithful) [3]

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
Jesus shall reign where'er the sun
Does his successive journeys run;
His kingdom stretch from shore to shore
Till moons shall wax and wane no more.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
For Him shall endless prayer be made,
And praises throng to crown His head;
His Name, like sweet perfume shall rise
With every morning sacrifice.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
People and realms of every tongue
Dwell on His love with sweetest song;
And infant voices shall proclaim
Their early blessings on His Name.

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
Blessings abound where'er He reigns;
The prisoner leaps to lose his chains,
The weary find eternal rest,
And all the sons of want are blest.

parts.label: Verse 5
parts.lyrics:
Where He displays His healing power
Death and the curse are known no more;
In Him the tribes of Adam boast
More blessings than their father lost.

parts.label: Verse 6
parts.lyrics:
Let every creature rise and bring
Peculiar honors to our King,
Angels descend with songs again,
And earth repeat the loud Amen.

hymns.title: Jesus Sinners Doth Receive
hymns.words: Erdmann Neumeister, 1718.  Translated by Henry Mills, 1845 (et al).
hymns.music: 'Meinen Jesum Lass` Ich Nicht (Darmstadt)' from Neu-verfertigtes Darmstädtiches Gesang-Buch, 1699.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
Jesus sinners doth receive;
Well may we this saying ponder
Who in sin's delusions live,
And from God and Heaven wander:
Here is hope for all who grieve-
Jesus sinners doth receive.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
We deserve but grief and shame,-
Yet His words, rich grace revealing,
Pardon, peace, and life proclaim;
Here their ills have perfect healing
Who with humble hearts believe-
Jesus sinners doth receive.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
As the shepherd seeks to find
His lost sheep that from Him strayeth,
So hath Christ each soul in mind,
And for its salvation prayeth;
Fain He'd have each wand'rer live:
Jesus sinners doth receive.

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
Come, then, all by guilt oppressed,
Jesus calls, and He would make you
God's own children, pure and blest,
And to glory He would take you;
Think on this, and well believe
Jesus sinners doth receive.

parts.label: Verse 5
parts.lyrics:
Savior, now I come to Thee:
Great my sins, a weary burden!
Wilt Thou mercy show to me?
Can I hope to find a pardon?
I will trust: my soul relieve!
Me, a sinner, Lord, receive!

parts.label: Verse 6
parts.lyrics:
Rich Thy mercy-strangely good! O how oft have I offended!
But through Thy redeeming blood All my fear of wrath is ended:
Yes I now can witness give: Jesus sinners doth receive!

parts.label: Verse 7
Verse 8
parts.lyrics:
Jesus sinners doth receive! Happy in His ceaseless favor,
Here for Heaven I will live, There shall live with Him forever,
"Joy in death these tidings give; Jesus sinners doth receive!"

hymns.title: Jesus Wants All Of His Children
hymns.words: verses 1-5 Mrs. James W. Wood, 1909. verses 6-7 Brian J. Dumont, 2008.
hymns.music: 'Blessed Are They' Mrs. James W. Wood, from "Service in Song", Standard Pub. Co., 1909.
topics: Children (see also God's Children - the Faithful)
God's Children - the Faithful (see also Saints, People of the World)
Submission (see also Following Jesus, God - Providence of, Trust)

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
Jesus wants all of His children
to be good and true;
He will help if we but ask Him,
help us gladly too.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
Jesus was so meek and lowly,
As a little child.
We will try to be like Jesus,
gentle, patient, mild.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
Jesus wants us to be loving,
helping when we may.
We will try to be kindhearted,
merciful each day.

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
"Blessed are the pure in heart,"
thus the Savior taught.
Clean in mind, in soul, in body,
pure in every thought.

parts.label: Verse 5
parts.lyrics:
When we find our friends are angry,
we will to them say,
"Jesus wants you to be loving,
each and every day."

parts.label: Verse 6
parts.lyrics:
When I know that I have done wrong, to Jesus I flee.
He has paid for all transgressions, He has paid for me!

parts.label: Verse 7
parts.lyrics:
Jesus knew that we would fail Him so He came to be
Life to all the poor and lost ones, life eternally!

hymns.title: Jesus, In Thy Dying Woes
hymns.tune: Words on the Cross - The Litany
hymns.music: 'Words on the Cross - The Litany' William H. Monk, 1889. Setting: "A Hymnal" (Episcopal), 1916.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
Jesus, in Thy dying woes,
Even while Thy lifeblood flows,
Craving pardon for Thy foes;
Hear us, holy Jesus.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
Savior, for our pardon sue,
When our sins Thy pangs renew,
For we know not what we do:
Hear us, holy Jesus.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
O may we, who mercy need,
Be like Thee in heart and deed,
When with wrong our spirits bleed:
Hear us, holy Jesus.

hymns.title: Jesus, King of Glory
hymns.music: 'St. Alban' Franz Joseph Haydn, 1774.  Setting: John Bacchus Dykes, 1868.
topics: Children (see also God's Children - the Faithful)

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
Jesus, King of glory, throned above the sky, Jesus, tender Savior, hear Thy children cry.
Pardon our transgressions, cleanse us from our sin,
By Thy Spirit help us heav'nly life to win.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
On this day of gladness,
Bending low the knee
In thine earthly temple, Lord, we worship thee;
Celebrate thy goodness,
Mercy, grace, and truth,
All thy loving guidance
Of our heedless youth.

parts.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
Help us ever steadfast in the faith to be:
In Thy Church's conflicts fighting valiantly.
Loving Savior, strengthen these weak hearts of ours,
Through Thy cross to conquer crafty evil powers.

parts.label: Verse 5
Verse 6
Refrain
parts.lyrics: Jesus, King of glory, throned above the sky, Jesus, tender Savior, hear Thy children cry.

hymns.title: Jesus, Tender Shepherd, Hear Me
hymns.music: 'Evening Prayer' John Stainer, 1898.

parts.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
All this day thy hand has led me,
And I thank Thee for Thy care;
Thou hast clothed me, warmed and fed me,
Listen to my evening prayer.

parts.label: Verse 3

hymns.title: Jesus, Thy Boundless Love To Me
hymns.words: Paul Gerhardt, 1653.  Translated by John Wesley, 1739.
hymns.music: 'Yoakley' William Yoakley, 1820.  Setting: "The Lute of Zion", 1853.

parts.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
O, grant that nothing in my soul
May dwell but Thy pure love alone!
Oh, may Thy love possess me whole,
My joy, my treasure, and my crown!
All coldness from my heart remove;
My every act, word, thought, be love.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
O love, how cheering is thy ray!
All pain before thy presence flies;
Care, anguish, sorrow, melt away
Where'er thy healing beams arise.
O Jesus, nothing may I see,
Nothing desire or seek, but Thee!

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
This love unwearied I pursue
And dauntlessly to Thee aspire.
Oh, may Thy love my hope renew
Burn in my soul like heav'nly fire!
And day and night be all my care
To guard this sacred treasure there.

parts.label: Verse 5

hymns.title: Joy to the World
hymns.music: 'Antioch' pieced together from "Messiah" George F. Handel, 1741.  Setting: Lowell Mason, 1836.
topics: God's Children - the Faithful (see also Saints, People of the World)

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
Joy to the world, the Lord is come!
Let earth receive her King;
Let ev'ry heart prepare Him room,
And Heav'n and nature sing,
And Heav'n and nature sing,
And Heav'n, and Heav'n, and nature sing.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
Joy to the earth, the Savior reigns!
Let men their songs employ;
While fields and floods, rocks, hills and plains
Repeat the sounding joy,
Repeat the sounding joy,
Repeat, repeat, the sounding joy.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
No more let sins and sorrows grow,
Nor thorns infest the ground;
He comes to make His blessings flow
Far as the curse is found,
Far as the curse is found,
Far as, far as, the curse is found.

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
He rules the world with truth and grace,
And makes the nations prove
The glories of His righteousness,
And wonders of His love,
And wonders of His love,
And wonders, wonders, of His love.

hymns.title: Joyful, Joyful, We Adore Thee
hymns.music: 'Ode to Joy' Ludwig van Beethoven; Adapted by Edward Hodges, 1824.

parts.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
All Thy works with joy surround Thee,
earth and heaven reflect Thy rays,
Stars and angels sing around Thee,
center of unbroken praise.
Field and forest, vale and mountain,
flowery meadow, flashing sea,
Singing bird and flowing fountain
call us to rejoice in Thee.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
Thou art giving and forgiving,
ever blessing, ever blessed,
Wellspring of the joy of living,
ocean depth of happy rest!
Thou our Father, Christ our Brother,
all who live in love are Thine;
Teach us how to love each other,
lift us to the joy divine.

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
Mortals, join the happy chorus,
which the morning stars began;
Father love is reigning o'er us,
brother love binds man to man.
Ever singing, march we onward,
victors in the midst of strife,
Joyful music leads us Sunward
in the triumph song of life.

hymns.title: Lamp of Our Feet
hymns.music: 'St. Agnes' John B. Dykes, 1866.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
Lamp of our feet! whereby we trace
Our path, when wont to stray;
Stream from the fount of heav'nly grace!
Brook by the trav'ler's way!

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
Bread of our souls! whereon we feed;
True manna from on high!
Our guide, and chart wherein we read
Of realms beyond the sky.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
Pillar of fire- through watches dark!
Or radiant cloud by day!
When waves would whelm our tossing bark-
Our anchor and our stay!

parts.label: Verse 4
Verse 5
parts.lyrics:
Riches in poverty! our aid
In every needful hour!
Unshaken rock! the pilgrim's shade;
The soldier's fortress tow'r.

parts.label: Verse 6
parts.lyrics:
Our shield and buckler in the fight!
Vict'ry's triumphant palm!
Comfort in grief! in weakness, might!
In sickness, Gilead's balm.

parts.label: Verse 7
parts.lyrics:
Childhood's preceptor! manhood's trust!
Old age's firm ally!
Our hope-when we go down to dust,
Of immortality.

parts.label: Verse 8
parts.lyrics:
Pure oracles of truth divine!
Unlike each fabled dream
Given forth from Delphos' mystic shrine
Or groves of Academe!

parts.label: Verse 9
parts.lyrics:
Word of the ever-living God!
Will of His glorious Son!
Without Thee, how could earth be trod?
Or Heaven itself be won?

parts.label: Verse 10
parts.lyrics:
Yet to unfold thy hidden worth,
Thy mysteries to reveal,
That Spirit which first gave thee forth,
Thy volume must unseal!

parts.label: Verse 11
parts.lyrics:
And we, if we aright would learn
The wisdom it imparts,
Must to its heavenly teaching turn
With simple, child-like hearts!

hymns.title: Let All Mortal Flesh Keep Silence
hymns.words: from Liturgy of St. James, 4th Century.  Translated by Gerard Moultrie, 1864.
hymns.music: 'Picardy' traditional French.  Setting: "The English Hymnal", 1906, alt.
topics: Submission (see also Following Jesus, God - Providence of, Trust) [1]

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
Let all mortal flesh keep silence,
And with fear and trembling stand;
Ponder nothing earthly minded,
For with blessing in His hand,
Christ our God to earth descendeth,
Our full homage to demand.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
King of kings, yet born of Mary,
As of old on earth He stood,
Lord of lords, in human vesture,
In the body and the blood;
He will give to all the faithful
His own self for heav'nly food.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
Rank on rank the host of heaven
Spreads its vanguard on the way,
As the Light of light descendeth
From the realms of endless day,
That the pow'rs of hell may vanish
As the darkness clears away.

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
At His feet the six wingèd seraph,
Cherubim with sleepless eye,
Veil their faces to the presence,
As with ceaseless voice they cry:
Alleluia, Alleluia
Alleluia, Lord Most High!

hymns.title: Let Children Hear The Mighty Deeds
hymns.music: 'Lea' James Lea Summers, (1837-1881).
topics: Children (see also God's Children - the Faithful)
God's Children - the Faithful (see also Saints, People of the World)

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
Let children hear the mighty deeds
Which God performed of old;
Which in our younger years we saw,
And which our fathers told.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
He bids us make His glories known,
His works of pow'r and grace;
And we'll convey His wonders down
Through every rising race.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
Our lips shall tell them to our sons,
And they again to theirs;
That generations yet unborn
May teach them to their heirs.

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
Thus shall they learn in God alone
Their hope securely stands,
That they may ne'er forget His work
But practice His commands.

hymns.title: Let Our Gladness Have No End
hymns.words: From the Kancional, by Tobias Zavorka, 1602.  Translator unknown.
hymns.music: 'Narodil se Kristus Pán' or 'Salvator Natus' 15th Century Bohemian.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
Let our gladness have no end,
Hallelujah! For to earth did Christ descend.
Hallelujah!

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
See, the loveliest blooming rose,
Hallelujah! From the branch of
Jesse grows. Hallelujah!

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
Into flesh is made the Word.
Hallelujah! He, our refuge and our Lord.
Hallelujah!

parts.label: Refrain
parts.lyrics: On this day God gave us Christ, His Son, to save us; Christ, His Son, to save us.

hymns.title: Lift High The Cross
hymns.words: George W. Kitchin (1827-1912). Modified by Michael R. Newbolt, 1916.
hymns.music: 'Crucifier' Sydney H. Nicholson, 1916.  Setting: "Hymns Ancient and Modern", 1922.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
Come, brethren, follow where our
Captain trod, our King victorious, Christ the Son of God.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
Led on their way by this triumphant sign,
The hosts of God in conquering ranks combine.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
Each newborn servant of the
Crucified Bears on the brow the seal of Him Who died.

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
This is the sign which
Satan's legions fear and angels veil their faces to revere.

parts.label: Verse 5
parts.lyrics:
Saved by this
Cross whereon their Lord was slain, the sons of
Adam their lost home regain.

parts.label: Refrain
parts.lyrics:
Lift high the cross, the love of Christ proclaim,
Till all the world adore His sacred
Name.

hymns.title: Lift Up Your Heads, Ye Mighty Gates
hymns.words: Georg Weissel, 1642. Translated by Catherine Winkworth, 1855.
hymns.music: 'Milwaukee' or 'Macht hoch die Tür (Lemke)' August Lemke, 1849.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
Lift up your heads, ye mighty gates!
Behold, the King of glory waits;
The King of kings is drawing near,
The Savior of the world is here;
Life and salvation doth He bring,
Wherefore rejoice and gladly sing:
We praise Thee, Father, now!
Creator, wise art Thou!

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
The Lord is just, a Helper tried,
Mercy is ever at His side,
His kingly crown is holiness,
His scepter, pity in distress,
The end of all our woe He brings;
Wherefore the earth is glad and sings:
We praise Thee, Savior, now!
Mighty in deed art Thou!

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
O blest the land, the city blest,
Where Christ the Ruler is confessed!
O happy hearts and happy homes
To whom this King in triumph comes!
The cloudless Sun of joy He is,
Who bringeth pure delight and bliss.
O Comforter divine,
What boundless grace is Thine!

parts.label: Verse 4
Verse 5
parts.lyrics:
Redeemer, come! I open wide
My heart to Thee; here, Lord, abide!
Let me Thy inner presence feel,
Thy grace and love in me reveal.
Thy Holy Spirit guide us on,
Until our glorious goal be won!
Eternal praise and fame
We offer to Thy Name.

hymns.title: Lo, God To Heav'n Ascendeth
hymns.words: Gottfried Wilhelm Sacer, 1661.  verses 1-5,7 Translated by Frances Elizabeth Cox, 1841.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
Lo, God to Heav'n ascendeth!
Throughout its regions vast
With shouts triumphant blendeth
the trumpet's thrilling blast:
Sing praise to Christ the Lord;
sing praise with exultation,
King of each heathen nation,
the God of Hosts adored!

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
With joy is Heav'n resounding
Christ's glad return to see;
Behold the saints surrounding
the Lord who set them free.
Bright myriads, thronging, come;
the cherub band rejoices,
And loud seraphic voices
Welcome Messiah home.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
No more the way is hidden,
Since Christ our Head arose:
No more to man forbidden
The road to Heav'n that goes.
Our Lord is gone before;
yet here He will not leave us,
And soon in Heav'n receive us
and open wide the door.

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
Christ is our place preparing;
to Heav'n we, too, shall rise,
And, joys angelic sharing,
Be where our treasure lies:
There may each heart be found!
Where Jesus Christ has entered,
There let our Hope be centered;
Our course still heav'nward bound.

parts.label: Verse 5
parts.lyrics:
May we, His servants, thither
In heart and mind ascend,
And let us sing together:
"We seek Thee, Christ, our friend,
Thee, God's exalted Son,
our Life, and Way to Heaven,
To whom all pow'r is given,
our Joy and Hope and Crown."

hymns.title: Lo, How A Rose E'er Blooming
hymns.words: verses 1-2, 15th Century German.  Translated by Theodore Baker, 1894.
hymns.music: 'Es Ist Ein Ros Entsprungen (Rhythmic)' German from Köln, 1599.  Setting: Michael Praetorius, 1609.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
Lo, how a Rose e'er blooming
from tender stem hath sprung!
Of Jesse's lineage coming,
as men of old have sung.
It came, a flow'ret bright,
amid the cold of winter,
When half spent was the night.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
Isaiah 'twas foretold it,
the Rose I have in mind;
With Mary we behold it,
the virgin mother kind.
To show God's love aright,
she bore to men a Savior,
When half spent was the night.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
The shepherds heard the story
proclaimed by angels bright,
How Christ, the Lord of glory
was born on earth this night.
To Bethlehem they sped
and in the manger found Him,
As angel heralds said.

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
This Flow'r, whose fragrance tender
with sweetness fills the air,
Dispels with glorious splendor
the darkness everywhere;
True Man, yet very God,
from sin and death He saves us,
And lightens ev'ry load.

parts.label: Verse 5
parts.lyrics:
O Savior, Child of Mary,
who felt our human woe,
O Savior, King of glory,
who dost our weakness know;
Bring us at length we pray,
to the bright courts of Heaven,
And to the endless day!

hymns.title: Lo! He Comes With Clouds Descending
hymns.words: John Cennick, 1752. Altered by Charles Wesley, 1758, alt.
hymns.music: 'Helmsley' attr. Thomas Olivers, 1765.  Setting: "The English Hymnal", 1906, alt.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
Lo! He comes with clouds descending,
Once for ev'ry sinner slain;
Thousand thousand saints attending,
Swell the triumph of His train:
Hallelujah! Hallelujah! Hallelujah!
God appears on earth to reign.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
Ev'ry eye shall now behold Him
Robed in dreadful majesty;
Those who set at naught and sold Him,
Pierced and nailed Him to the tree,
Deeply wailing, deeply wailing, deeply wailing,
Shall the true Messiah see.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
Ev'ry island, sea, and mountain,
Heav'n and earth, shall flee away;
All who hate Him must, confounded,
Hear the trump proclaim the day:
Come to judgment! Come to judgment! Come to judgment!
Come to judgment! Come away!

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
Now redemption, long expected,
See in solemn pomp appear;
All His saints, by man rejected,
Now shall meet Him in the air:
Hallelujah! Hallelujah! Hallelujah!
See the day of God appear!

parts.label: Verse 5
parts.lyrics:
Answer Thine own bride and Spirit,
Hasten, Lord, the gen'ral doom!
The new Heav'n and earth inherit,
Take Thy pining exiles home:
All creation, all creation, all creation,
Travails! groans! and bids Thee come!

hymns.title: Look Down, O Lord, From Heaven Behold (Ach Gott vom Himmel)
hymns.words: Martin Luther, 1524. Translated by Frances Elizabeth Cox, 1864.
hymns.music: 'Ach Gott vom Himmel' from Erfurt Enchiridion, 1524.  Setting: Karl August Haupt, 1869.
topics: God's Children - the Faithful (see also Saints, People of the World)

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
Look down, O Lord, from heav'n behold,
And let thy pity waken!
How few the flock within thy fold,
Neglected and forsaken!
Almost thou'lt seek for faith in vain,
And those who should thy truth maintain
Thy Word from us have taken.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
With frauds which they themselves invent
Thy truth they have confounded;
Their hearts are not with one consent
On thy pure doctrine grounded;
And, whilst they gleam with outward show,
They lead thy people to and fro,
In error's maze astounded.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
God surely will uproot all those
With vain deceits who store us,
With haughty tongue who God oppose,
And say, "Who'll stand before us?
By right or might we will prevail;
What we determine cannot fail,
For who can lord it o'er us?"

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
For this, saith God, I will arise,
These wolves my flock are rending;
I've heard my people's bitter sighs
To heav'n my throne ascending:
Now will I up, and set at rest
Each weary soul by fraud opprest,
The poor with might defending.

parts.label: Verse 5
parts.lyrics:
The silver sev'n times tried is pure
From all adulteration;
So, through God's word, shall men endure
Each trial and temptation:
Its worth gleams brighter through the cross,
And, purified from human dross,
It shines through every nation.

parts.label: Verse 6

hymns.title: Look Down, O Lord, From Heaven Behold (Es ist das Heil uns Kommen Her)
hymns.tune: Es ist das Heil uns Kommen Her
hymns.words: Martin Luther, 1524. Translated by Frances Elizabeth Cox, 1864.
hymns.music: 'Es ist das Heil uns Kommen Her'

hymns.title: Lord Jesus Think On Me
hymns.words: Synesius of Cyrene, circa 430.  Translated by Allen W. Chatfield, 1876.
hymns.music: 'Southwell' William Daman's Psalter, 1579.  Setting: "Common Service Book" (ULCA), 1917.
topics: Submission (see also Following Jesus, God - Providence of, Trust) [1-4]

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
Lord Jesus, think on me
And purge away my sin;
From earthborn passions set me free
And make me pure within.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
Lord Jesus, think on me,
With many'a care oppressed;
Let me Thy loving servant be
And taste Thy promised rest.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
Lord Jesus, think on me
Amid the battle's strife;
In all my pain and misery
Be Thou my Health and Life.

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
Lord Jesus, think on me
Nor let me go astray;
Through darkness and perplexity
Point Thou the heav'nly way.

parts.label: Verse 5
parts.lyrics:
Lord Jesus, think on me
When floods the tempest high;
When on doth rush the enemy,
O Savior, be Thou nigh!

parts.label: Verse 6
parts.lyrics:
Lord Jesus, think on me
That, when the flood is past,
I may th'eternal brightness see
And share Thy joy at last.

parts.label: Verse 7
parts.lyrics:
Lord Jesus, think on me
That I may sing above
To Father, Spirit, and to Thee
The strains of praise and love.

hymns.title: Lord of Glory, Who Hast Bought Us
hymns.music: 'HyFrydol' Rowland H. Prichard, 1830.  Setting: "The English Hymnal", 1906.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
Lord of Glory, who hast bought us
with Thy lifeblood as the price,
Never grudging for the lost ones
that tremendous sacrifice;
And with that hast freely given
blessings countless as the sand,
To th'unthankful and the evil
with Thine own unsparing hand.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
Grant us hearts, dear Lord, to yield Thee
gladly, freely, of Thine own.
With the sunshine of Thy goodness
melt our thankless hearts of stone.
Till our cold and selfish natures,
warmed by Thee, at length believe
That more happy and more blessed
'tis to give than to receive.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
Wondrous honor hast Thou given
to our humblest charity.
In Thine own mysterious sentence,
"Ye have done it unto Me."
Can it be, O gracious Master,
Thou dost deign for alms to sue,
Saying by Thy poor and needy,
"Give as I have given you"

parts.label: Verse 4

hymns.title: Lord of Life, All Praise Excelling
hymns.music: 'HyFrydol' Rowland H. Prichard, 1830.  Setting: "The English Hymnal", 1906.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
Lord of life, all praise excelling,
Thou, in glory unconfined,
Deignst to make Thy humble dwelling
With the poor of humble mind.
As Thy love, through all creation,
Beams like Thy diffusive light;
So the high and humble station
Both are equal in Thy sight.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
Thus Thy care, for all providing,
Warmed Thy faithful prophet's tongue;
Who, the lot of all deciding,
To Thy chosen Israel sung.
When Thy harvest yields Thee pleasure,
Thou the golden sheaf shalt bind;
To the poor belongs the treasure
Of the scattered ears behind.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
Still we read Thy Word declaring
Mercy, Lord, Thine own decree;
Mercy ev'ry sorrow sharing,
Warms the heart resembling Thee.
Still the orphan and the stranger,
Still the widow owns Thy care;
Screened by Thee in ev'ry danger,
Heard by Thee in ev'ry prayer.

hymns.title: Lord Of Our Life
hymns.words: Matthäus Apelles von Löwenstern, 1644.  Translated by Philip Pusey, 1840.
hymns.music: 'Iste Confessor' or 'Rouen' from Poitiers Antiphoner, 1746.
topics: God's Children - the Faithful (see also Saints, People of the World)

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
Lord of our life, and God of our salvation,
Star of our night, and Hope of every nation,
Hear and receive Thy church's supplication,
Lord God Almighty.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
See round Thine Ark the hungry billows curling!
See how Thy foes their banners are unfurling!
Lord, while their darts envenomed they are hurling,
Thou canst preserve us.

parts.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
Peace, in our hearts, our evil thoughts assuaging,
Peace, in Thy Church, where brothers are engaging,
Peace, when the world its busy war is waging;
Calm Thy foes raging!

parts.label: Verse 5

hymns.title: Lord Who Throughout These Forty Days
hymns.music: 'St. Flavian' Day's Psalter, 1563.
topics: Submission (see also Following Jesus, God - Providence of, Trust) [3]

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
Lord, who throughout these forty days
For us didst fast and pray,
Teach us with Thee to mourn our sins
And close by Thee to stay.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
As Thou with Satan didst contend,
And didst the vict'ry win,
O give us strength in Thee to fight,
In Thee to conquer sin.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
As Thou didst hunger bear, and thirst,
So teach us, gracious Lord,
To die to self, and chiefly live
By Thy most holy Word.

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
And through these days of penitence,
And through Thy passiontide,
Yea, evermore in life and death,
Jesus, with us abide.

parts.label: Verse 5
parts.lyrics:
Abide with us, that so, this life
Of suff'ring over past,
An Easter of unending joy
We may attain at last.

hymns.title: Lord, Dismiss Us With Thy Blessing
hymns.words: John Fawcett, 1773; verse 3 alt. by Godfrey Thring, 1880.
hymns.music: 'Regent Square' Henry Smart, 1867.  Setting: "Psalms and Hymns for Divine Worship", 1867.

parts.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
Thanks we give and adoration
For Thy Gospel's joyful sound;
May the fruits of Thy salvation
In our hearts and lives abound.
Ever faithful, ever faithful,
To the truth may we be found.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
So that when Thy love shall call us,
Savior, from the world away,
Fear of death shall not appall us,
Glad Thy summons to obey.
May we ever, may we ever,
Reign with Thee in endless day.

hymns.title: Lord, Enthroned in Heavenly Splendor
hymns.music: 'Bryn Calfaria' William Owen, 1852.  Setting: "The English Hymnal", 1906.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
Lord, enthroned in heav'nly splendor,
First begotten from the dead,
You alone, our strong
Defender, Now lift up
Your people's head. Jesus, true and living
Bread! Jesus, true and living
Bread!

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
Here our humblest homage pay we,
Here in loving reference bow;
Here for faith's discernment pray we,
Lest we fail to know
You now. Thou art here, we ask not how. Thou art here, we ask not how.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
Though the lowliest form doth veil Thee
As of old in Bethlehem,
Here as there Thine angels hail Thee,
Branch and Flow'r of
Jesse's stem. We in worship join with them.
We in worship join with them.

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
Paschal Lamb, Your offering finished
Once for all when
You were slain,
In its fullness undiminished
Shall forevermore remain.
Cleansing souls from every stain.
Cleansing souls from every stain.

parts.label: Verse 5
parts.lyrics:
Great High Priest of our profession,
Through the veil Thou wentest in,
By Thy mighty intercession,
Grace and peace for us to win. Jesus, true and living
Bread! Jesus, true and living
Bread!

parts.label: Verse 6
parts.lyrics:
Life imparting heavenly Manna,
Smitten Rock with streaming side,
Heaven and earth with loud hosanna
Worship You, the Lamb Who died.
Alleluia! Alleluia! Alleluia!
Risen, Ascended, Glorified!

parts.label: Refrain
parts.lyrics: Alleluia! Alleluia! Alleluia!

hymns.title: Lord, Keep Us Steadfast in Thy Word
hymns.tune: Erhalt Uns, Herr, bei deinem Wort
hymns.words: Martin Luther, 1541.  Translated by Catherine Winkworth, 1863.
hymns.music: 'Erhalt Uns, Herr, bei deinem Wort' from Klug's "Geistliche Lieder auffs new gebessert", 1543.
topics: God's Children - the Faithful (see also Saints, People of the World)

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
Lord, keep us steadfast in Thy Word;
Curb those who fain by craft and sword
Would wrest the kingdom from Thy Son
And set at naught all He hath done.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
Lord Jesus Christ, Thy pow'r make known,
For Thou art Lord of lords alone;
Defend Thy Christendom that we
May evermore sing praise to Thee.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
O Comforter of priceless worth,
Send peace and unity on earth.
Support us in our final strife
And lead us out of death to life.

hymns.title: Lord, Thee I Love with All My Heart
hymns.tune: Herzlich Lieb hab ich Dich O Herr
hymns.words: Martin Schalling, circa 1571.  Translated by Catherine Winkworth, 1858.
hymns.music: 'Herzlich Lieb hab ich Dich O Herr' Strassburg, 1577.  Setting: "Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book", 1931.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
Lord, Thee I love with all my heart;
I pray Thee, ne'er from me depart;
With tender mercy cheer me.
Earth has no pleasure I would share,
Yea, Heav'n itself were void and bare
If Thou, Lord, wert not near me.
And should my heart for sorrow break,
My trust in Thee can nothing shake.
Thou art the portion I have sought;
Thy precious blood my soul has bought.
Lord Jesus Christ, My God and Lord,
my God and Lord,
Forsake me not! I trust Thy Word.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
Yea, Lord, 'twas Thy rich bounty gave
My body, soul, and all I have
In this poor life of labor.
Lord, grant that I in every place
May glorify Thy lavish grace
And serve and help my neighbor.
Let no false doctrine me beguile,
Let Satan not my soul defile.
Give strength and patience unto me
To bear my cross and follow Thee.
Lord Jesus Christ, My God and Lord,
my God and Lord,
In death Thy comfort still afford.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
Lord, let at last Thine angels come,
To Abr'am's bosom bear me home,
That I may die unfearing;
And in its narrow chamber keep
My body safe in peaceful sleep
Until Thy reappearing.
And then from death awaken me,
That these mine eyes with joy may see,
O Son of God, Thy glorious face,
My Savior and my fount of grace.
Lord Jesus Christ, My prayer attend,
my prayer attend,
And I will praise Thee without end!

hymns.title: Lord, Who at Cana's Wedding Feast
hymns.music: 'St. Ursula' Frederick Westlake, 1863.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
Lord, who at Cana's wedding feast
Didst as a Guest appear,
Thou dearer far than earthly guest,
Vouchsafe Thy presence here.
For holy Thou indeed dost prove
The marriage vow to be,
Proclaiming it a type of love
Between the Church and Thee.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
The holiest vow that man can make,
The golden thread in life,
The bond that none may dare to break,
That bindeth man and wife,
Which, blest by Thee, whate'er betide,
No evil shall destroy,
Through careworn days each care divides
And doubles every joy.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
On those who at Thine altar kneel,
O Lord, Thy blessing pour,
That each may wake the other's zeal
To love Thee more and more.
Oh, grant them here in peace to live,
In purity and love,
And, this world leaving, to receive
A crown of life above.

hymns.title: May God Bestow on Us His Grace
hymns.words: Martin Luther, 1524.  Translated by Richard Massie, 1854, alt.
hymns.music: 'Es Wollt uns Gott Genædig' adapted from older German hymn by Martin Luther. Found in Erfurt Enchiridion, 1524.
topics: God's Children - the Faithful (see also Saints, People of the World)

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
May God bestow on us His grace,
With blessings rich provide us,
And may the brightness of His face
To life eternal guide us
That we His saving health may know,
His gracious will and pleasure,
And also to the heathen show
Christ's riches without measure
And unto God convert them.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
Thine over all shall be the praise
And thanks of every nation,
And all the world with joy shall raise
The voice of exultation;
For Thou shalt judge the earth, O Lord,
Nor suffer sin to flourish;
Thy people's pasture is Thy Word
Their souls to feed and nourish,
In righteous paths to keep them.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
Oh, let the people praise Thy worth,
In all good works increasing;
The land shall plenteous fruit bring forth,
Thy Word is rich in blessing.
May God the Father, God the Son,
And God the Spirit bless us!
Let all the world praise Him alone,
Let solemn awe possess us.
Now let our hearts say, Amen.

hymns.title: Moment By Moment
hymns.music: 'Whittle' May Whittle Moody, 1893.

parts.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
Never a trial that He is not there,
Never a burden that He doth not bear,
Never a sorrow that He doth not share,
Moment by moment,
I'm under His care.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
Never a heartache, and never a groan,
Never a teardrop and never a moan;
Never a danger but there on the throne,
Moment by moment He thinks of His own.

parts.label: Verse 4
Refrain

hymns.title: More Love to Thee
hymns.music: 'More Love to Thee' William Howard Doane, 1870.  Setting: William Howard Doane, 1870, alt.

parts.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
Then shall my latest breath, Whisper Thy praise,
This be the parting cry My heart shall raise;
This still its pray'r shall be, More love, O Christ, to Thee,
More love to Thee; More love to Thee.

hymns.title: My Faith Looks Up To Thee
hymns.music: 'Olivet' Lowell Mason, 1832.
topics: Submission (see also Following Jesus, God - Providence of, Trust)

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
My faith looks up to Thee,
Thou Lamb of Calvary,
Savior divine!
Now hear me while I pray,
take all my guilt away,
O let me from this day
be wholly Thine!

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
May Thy rich grace impart
Strength to my fainting heart,
my zeal inspire!
As Thou hast died for me,
O may my love to Thee,
Pure warm, and changeless be,
a living fire!

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
While life's dark maze I tread,
And griefs around me spread,
be Thou my Guide;
Bid darkness turn to day,
wipe sorrow's tears away,
Nor let me ever stray
from Thee aside.

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
When ends life's transient dream,
When death's cold sullen stream
over me roll;
Blest Savior, then in love,
fear and distrust remove;
O bear me safe above,
a ransomed soul!

hymns.title: My Hope Is Built
hymns.music: 'Melita' John Bacchus Dykes, 1861.  Setting: "Hymns Ancient and Modern", 1869.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
My hope is built on nothing less
Than Jesus' blood and righteousness. I dare not trust the sweetest frame,
But wholly trust in Jesus'
Name.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
When darkness veils His lovely face, I rest on His unchanging grace.
In every high and stormy gale, My anchor holds within the veil.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
His oath, His covenant, His blood,
Support me in the whelming flood.
When all around my soul gives way, He then is all my hope and stay.

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
When He shall come with trumpet sound,
Oh may I then in Him be found.
Dressed in His righteousness alone,
Faultless to stand before the throne.

parts.label: Refrain
parts.lyrics:
On Christ the solid
Rock I stand,
All other ground is sinking sand.

hymns.title: My Jesus, As Thou Wilt
hymns.words: Benjamin Schmolck, circa 1704.  Translated by Jane L. Borthwick, 1854.
hymns.music: 'Jewett' or 'Weber' Carl M. von Weber, 1821.  Setting: "Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book", 1931.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
My Jesus, as Thou wilt!
Oh, may Thy will be mine!
Into Thy hand of love
I would my all resign;
Through sorrow, or through joy,
conduct me as Thine own,
And help me still to say,
my Lord, Thy will be done!

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
My Jesus, as Thou wilt!
If needy here and poor,
Give me Thy people's bread,
their portion rich and sure.
The manna of Thy Word
Let my soul feed upon;
And if all else should fail,
my Lord, thy will be done!

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
My Jesus, as Thou wilt!
Though seen through many'a tear,
Let not my star of hope
grow dim or disappear;
Since Thou on earth hast wept,
and sorrowed oft alone,
If I must weep with Thee,
my Lord, Thy will be done!

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
My Jesus, as Thou wilt!
All shall be well for me;
Each changing future scene
I gladly trust with Thee:
Straight to my home above
I travel calmly on,
And sing, in life or death,
my Lord, Thy will be done!

hymns.title: My Savior's Love
hymns.music: 'My Savior`s Love' or 'I Stand Amazed in the Presence' Charles H. Gabriel, 1905.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
I stand amazed in the presence
Of Jesus the
Nazarene, And wonder how He could love me,
A sinner, condemn'd, unclean.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
For me it was in the garden He pray'd
"Not my will, but Thine;" He had no tears for His own griefs,
But sweat drops of blood for mine.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
In pity angels beheld Him,
And came from the world of light
To comfort Him in the sorrows, He bore for my soul that night.

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
When with the ransomed in glory His face I at last shall see,
'Twill be my joy thro' the ages,
To sing of His love for me.

parts.label: Refrain
parts.lyrics:
How marvelous! how wonderful!
And my song shall ever be:
How marvelous! how wonderful!
Is my Savior's love for me!

hymns.title: My Soul, Now Praise Thy Maker
hymns.words: Johann Graumann, 1525.  Translated by Catherine Winkworth, 1863.
hymns.music: 'Nun Lob, Mein Seel' from Johannes Kugelmann`s Concentus Novi, 1540
topics: Children (see also God's Children - the Faithful) [3,4]
God's Children - the Faithful (see also Saints, People of the World) [3,4]

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
My soul, now praise thy maker!
Let all within me bless His name
Who maketh thee partaker
Of mercies more than thou dar'st claim.
Forget Him not whose meekness
Still bears with all thy sin,
Who healeth all thy weakness,
Renews thy life within.
Whose grace and care are endless
And saved thee through the past;
Who leaves no suff'rer friendless,
But rights the wronged at last.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
He shows to man His treasure
Of judgment, truth, and righteousness,
His love beyond all measure,
His yearning pity o'er distress,
Nor treats us as we merit,
But lays His anger by.
The humble, contrite spirit
Finds His compassion nigh;
And high as Heav'n above us,
As break from close of day,
So far, since He doth love us,
He puts our sins away.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
For as a tender father
Hath pity on his children here,
He in His arms will gather
All who are His in childlike fear.
He knows how frail our powers
Who but from dust are made;
We flourish like the flowers,
And even so we fade;
The wind but o'er them passes,
And all their bloom is o'er-
We wither like the grasses,
Our place knows us no more.

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
God's grace alone endureth,
And children's children yet shall prove
How He with strength assureth
The hearts of all that seek His love.
In Heav'n is fixed His dwelling,
His rule is over all;
Angels, in might excelling,
Bright hosts, before Him fall.
Praise Him who ever reigneth,
All ye who hear His Word,
Nor our poor hymns disdaineth-
My soul, O praise the Lord!

hymns.title: Nearer, My God, To Thee
hymns.words: st. 1-2 by Sarah F. Adams, 1841. st. 3-5 by Hervey D. Ganse (1822-1891).
hymns.music: 'Bethany (Mason)' Lowell Mason, 1856.  Setting: Lowell Mason, 1859.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
Nearer, my God, to Thee,
nearer to Thee!
E'en though it be a cross
that raiseth me,
Still all my song shall be,
nearer, my God, to Thee.
Nearer, my God, to Thee,
Nearer to Thee!

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
Though like the wanderer,
the sun gone down,
Darkness be over me,
my rest a stone.
Yet in my dreams I'd be
nearer, my God to Thee.
Then evermore to be
Nearer to Thee!

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
Nearer, my Lord, to thee,
Nearer to thee!
Who to the cross didst come,
Dying for me!
Strengthen my willing feet,
Hold me in service sweet

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
Nearer, O Comforter,
Nearer to thee!
Who with my loving Lord
Dwellest with me!
Grant me thy fellowship!
Help me each day to keep

parts.label: Verse 5
parts.lyrics:
But to be nearer still,
Bring me, O God,
Not by the visioned steeps
Angels have trod.
Here where thy cross I see,
Jesus, I wait for thee,

parts.label: Verse 6
parts.lyrics:
There in my Father's home, safe and at rest,
There in my Savior's love, perfectly blest; Age
after age to be, nearer my God to Thee.

hymns.title: No, Not One!
hymns.music: 'No, Not One' George Crawford Hugg, 1894.  Setting: "Pentecostal Hymns, No. 2", 1894.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
There's not a friend like the lowly Jesus,
No, not one! no, not one!
None else could heal all our soul's diseases,
No, not one! no, not one!

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
No friend like Him is so high and holy,
No, not one! no, not one!
And yet no friend is so meek and lowly,
No, not one! no, not one!

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
There's not an hour that He is not near us,
No, not one! no, not one!
No night so dark but His love can cheer us,
No, not one! no, not one!

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
Did ever saint find this friend forsake him?
No, not one! no, not one!
Or sinner find that He would not take him?
No, not one! no, not one!

parts.label: Verse 5
parts.lyrics:
Was e'er a gift like the Savior given?
No, not one! no, not one!
Will He refuse us a home in heaven?
No, not one! no, not one!

parts.label: Refrain

hymns.title: None Other Lamb
hymns.music: 'Rossetti' William Jeater, 1907.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
None other Lamb, none other name,
None other hope in Heav'n or earth or sea,
None other hiding place from guilt and shame,
None beside Thee!

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
My faith burns low, my hope burns low;
Only my heart's desire cries out in me
By the deep thunder of its want and woe,
Cries out to Thee.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
Lord, Thou art life, though I be dead;
Love's fire Thou art, however cold I be:
Nor Heav'n have I, nor place to lay my head,
Nor home, but Thee.

hymns.title: Not Worthy, Lord, to Gather Up the Crumbs
hymns.music: 'Eventide' William H. Monk, 1861.  Setting: William H. Monk, 1861.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
Not worthy, Lord, to gather up the crumbs
With trembling hand that from Thy table fall,
A weary, heavy laden sinner comes
To plead Thy promise and obey Thy call.

parts.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
One word from Thee, my Lord, one smile, one look,
And I could face the cold, rough world again;
And with that treasure in my heart could brook
The wrath of devils and the scorn of men.

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
And is not mercy Thy prerogative-
Free mercy, boundless, fathomless, divine?
Me, Lord, the chief of sinners, me forgive,
And Thine the greater glory, only Thine.

parts.label: Verse 5
Verse 6
parts.lyrics:
My praise can only breathe itself in prayer,
My prayer can only lose itself in Thee;
Dwell Thou forever in my heart, and there,
Lord, let me sup with Thee; sup Thou with me.

hymns.title: Now Praise We Christ, the Holy One
hymns.words: Coelius Sedulius, circa 450.  Translated to German by Martin Luther, 1524.
hymns.music: 'Christum Wir Sollen Loben Schon' ancient Latin found in Erfurt Enchiridion, 1524.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
Now praise we Christ, the Holy One,
The spotless virgin Mary's Son,
Far as the blesséd sun doth shine
E'en to the world's remote confine

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
He, who Himself all things did make,
A servant's form vouchsafed to take,
That He as man mankind might win,
And save His creatures from their sin.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
The grace of God, th'Almighty Lord,
On the chaste mother was outpoured
a virgin pure and undefiled
In wondrous wise conceived a child.

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
The holy maid became th'abode
And temple of the living God;
And she, who knew not man, was blest
With God's own Word made manifest.

parts.label: Verse 5
parts.lyrics:
The noble mother bare a Son,
For so did Gabriel's promise run,
Whom John confessed and leapt with joy,
Ere yet the mother knew her boy.

parts.label: Verse 6
parts.lyrics:
In a rude manger, stretched on hay, In poverty content He lay;
With milk was fed the Lord of all, Who feeds the ravens when they call.

parts.label: Verse 7
parts.lyrics:
Th' angelic choir rejoice, and raise Their voice to God in songs of praise;
To humble shepherds is proclaimed The Shepherd who the world hath framed.

parts.label: Verse 8
parts.lyrics:
Honor to Thee, O Christ, be paid, Pure offspring of a holy maid,
With Father and with Holy Ghost, Till time in time's abyss be lost.

hymns.title: Now Rest Beneath Night's Shadow
hymns.music: 'Innsbruck' or 'Nun ruhen alle Wälder' or 'O Welt, Ich Muss Dich Lassen' Heinrich Isaac, 1490.

parts.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
The radiant sun hath vanished,
His golden rays are banished
By night, the foe of day;
But Christ, the Sun of gladness,
Dispelling all my sadness,
Within my heart holds constant sway.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
The rule of day is over
And shining jewels cover
The heaven's boundless blue.
Thus I shall shine in heaven,
Where crowns of gold are given
To all who faithful prove and true.

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
To rest my body hasteth,
Aside its garments casteth,
Types of mortality;
These I put off and ponder
How Christ will give me yonder
A robe of glorious majesty.

parts.label: Verse 5
parts.lyrics:
Lord Jesus, who dost love me,
Oh, spread Thy wings above me
And shield me from alarm!
Though evil would assail me,
Thy mercy will not fail me:
I rest in Thy protecting arm.

parts.label: Verse 6
parts.lyrics:
My loved ones, rest securely, For God this night will surely
From peril guard your heads. Sweet slumbers may He send you
And bid His hosts attend you And through the night watch o'er your beds.

hymns.title: Now Thank We All Our God
hymns.words: Martin Rinkart, c.1636. Translated Catherine Winkworth, 1856.
hymns.music: 'Nun Danket' Johann Crüger, 1647.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
Now thank we all our God,
with heart and hands and voices,
Who wondrous things has done,
in Whom this world rejoices;
Who from our mothers' arms
has blessed us on our way
With countless gifts of love,
and still is ours today.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
O may this bounteous God
through all our life be near us,
With ever joyful hearts
and blessed peace to cheer us;
And keep us in His grace,
and guide us when perplexed;
And free us from all ills,
in this world and the next!

parts.label: Verse 3

hymns.title: Now the Light Has Gone Away
hymns.tune: Müde bin ich, geh zur Ruh
hymns.music: 'Müde bin ich, geh zur Ruh' from Liederbuch für Kleinkinder-Schulen, 1842.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
Now the light has gone away;
Father, listen while I pray,
Asking Thee to watch and keep
And to send me quiet sleep.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
Jesus, Savior, wash away
All that has been wrong today;
Help me every day to be
Good and gentle, more like Thee.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
Let my near and dear ones be
Always near and dear to Thee.
Oh, bring me and all I love
To Thy happy home above.

parts.label: Verse 4
Verse 5
parts.lyrics:
Thou, my best and kindest Friend,
Thou wilt love me to the end.
Let me love Thee more and more,
Always better than before.

hymns.title: O Chief of Cities Bethlehem
hymns.words: Aurelius Clemens Prudentius (348-413). v. 1,2,4 Translated by N. B. Smithers, 1879,
hymns.music: 'Puer Nobis Nascitur' Michael Praetorius, 1609.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
O chief of cities, Bethlehem,
Of David's crown the fairest gem,
But more to us than David's name,
In you, as man, the Savior came.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
Beyond the sun in splendor bright,
Above you stands a wondrous light
Proclaiming from the conscious skies
That here, in flesh, the Godhead lies.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
The wise men, seeing Him so fair,
Bow low before Him, and with prayer
Their treasured eastern gifts unfold
Of incense, myrrh, and royal gold.

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
The golden tribute owns Him King,
But frankincense to God they bring,
And last, prophetic sign, with myrrh,
They shadow forth His sepulcher.

parts.label: Verse 5
parts.lyrics:
O Jesus, whom the Gentiles see,
With Father, Spirit, One in Three:
To You, O God, be glory giv'n
By saints on earth and saints in Heav'n.

hymns.title: O Come O Come Emmanuel
hymns.words: various, combined by unknown author approx 12th Century, Translated by John Mason Neale, 1851.
hymns.music: 'Veni Emmanuel' 15th Century French processional.  Setting: "Common Service Book" (ULCA), 1917.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
O come, O come, Emmanuel,
And ransom captive Israel,
That mourns in lonely exile here
Until the Son of God appear.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
O come, Thou
Wisdom from on high, Who orderest all things mightily;
To us the path of knowledge show,
And teach us in her ways to go.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
O come, Thou
Rod of Jesse, free Thine own from
Satan's tyranny; From depths of hell Thy people save,
And give them vict'ry ov'r the grave.

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
O come, Thou
Dayspring, come and cheer
Our spirits by Thine advent here;
Disperse the gloomy clouds of night,
And death's dark shadows put to flight.

parts.label: Verse 5
parts.lyrics:
O come, Thou
Key of David, come,
And open wide our heav'nly home;
Make safe the way that leads on high,
And close the path to misery.

parts.label: Refrain
parts.lyrics: Rejoice! Rejoice! Emmanuel shall come to thee, O Israel.

hymns.title: O Come, All Ye Faithful
hymns.words: John F. Wade, circa 1743. v.1-3, 6 Translated by Frederick Oakeley, 1841;
hymns.music: 'Adeste Fideles' or 'Portuguese Hymn' John F. Wade, 1743.  Setting: "A Hymnal" (Episcopal), 1916.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
O come, all ye faithful, joyful and triumphant, O come ye, O come ye, to Bethlehem.
Come and behold Him, born the King of angels; O

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
True God of true God,
Light from Light
Eternal, Lo, He shuns not the
Virgin's womb; Son of the Father, begotten, not created;

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
Sing, choirs of angels, sing in exultation; O sing, all ye citizens of heav'n above!
Glory to God, glory in the highest;

parts.label: Verse 4
Verse 5
parts.lyrics:
Lo! star led chieftains,
Magi, Christ adoring,
Offer Him incense, gold, and myrrh;
We to the Christ
Child bring our hearts' oblations.

parts.label: Refrain
parts.lyrics: come, let us adore Him, O come, let us adore Him, O come, let us adore Him, Christ the Lord.

hymns.title: O Day of Rest And Gladness
hymns.music: 'Woodbird' or 'Es Flog Ein Kleins Waldvögelein' traditional German found in

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
O day of rest and gladness,
o day of joy and light,
O balm of care and sadness,
most beautiful, most bright:
On thee, the high and lowly,
through ages joined in tune,
Sing holy, holy, holy,
to the great God Triune.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
On thee, at the creation,
the light first had its birth;
On thee, for our salvation,
Christ rose from depths of earth;
On thee, our Lord, victorious,
the Spirit sent from heaven,
And thus on thee, most glorious,
a triple light was given.

parts.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
Thou art a holy ladder,
where angels go and come;
Each Sunday finds us gladder,
nearer to heaven, our home;
A day of sweet refection,
thou art a day of love,
A day of resurrection
from earth to things above.

parts.label: Verse 5
parts.lyrics:
Today on weary nations
the heavenly manna falls;
To holy convocations
the silver trumpet calls,
Where Gospel light is glowing
with pure and radiant beams,
And living water flowing,
with soul refreshing streams.

parts.label: Verse 6
parts.lyrics:
New graces ever gaining from this our day of rest,
We reach the rest remaining to spirits of the blessed.
To Holy Ghost be praises, to Father, and to Son;
The church her voice upraises to Thee, blessed Three in One.

hymns.title: O Father, All Creating
hymns.music: 'Aurelia' Samuel Sebastian Wesley, 1864.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
O Father, all creating,
Whose wisdom, love, and pow'r
First bound two lives together
In Eden's primal hour,
Today to these Thy children
Thy earliest gifts renew:
A home by Thee made happy,
A love by Thee kept true.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
O Savior, Guest most bounteous
Of old in Galilee,
Vouchsafe today Thy presence
With these who call on Thee;
Their store of earthly gladness
Transform to heav'nly wine,
And teach them, in the tasting
To know the gift is Thine.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
O Spirit of the Father,
Breathe on them from above,
So mighty in Thy pureness,
So tender in Thy love;
That, guarded by Thy presence,
From sin and strife kept free,
Their lives may own Thy guidance,
Their hearts be rul'd by Thee.

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
Except Thou build it, Father,
The house is built in vain;
Except Thou, Savior, bless it,
The joy will turn to pain;
But naught can break the union
Of hearts in Thee made one,
And love Thy Spirit hallow'd
Is endless love begun.

hymns.title: O For A Thousand Tongues
hymns.music: 'Azmon' Carl G. Gläser, 1828.  Setting: Lowell Mason, 1839.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
O for a thousand tongues to sing
My great Redeemer's praise,
The glories of my God and King,
The triumphs of His grace!

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
My gracious Master and my God,
Assist me to proclaim,
To spread through all the earth abroad
The honors of Thy name.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
Jesus! the name that charms our fears,
That bids our sorrows cease;
'Tis music in the sinner's ears,
'Tis life, and health, and peace.

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
He breaks the pow'r of canceled sin,
He sets the prisoner free;
His blood can make the foulest clean,
His blood availed for me.

parts.label: Verse 5
parts.lyrics:
He speaks, and, listening to His voice,
New life the dead receive,
The mournful, broken hearts rejoice,
The humble poor believe.

parts.label: Verse 6
parts.lyrics:
Hear Him, ye deaf; His praise, ye dumb,
Your loosened tongues employ;
Ye blind, behold your Savior come,
And leap, ye lame, for joy.

parts.label: Verse 7
parts.lyrics:
In Christ your Head, you then shall know,
Shall feel your sins forgiven;
Anticipate your heaven below,
And own that love is heaven.

parts.label: Verse 8
parts.lyrics:
Glory to God, and praise and love
Be ever, ever given,
By saints below and saints above,
The church in earth and heaven.

parts.label: Verse 9
parts.lyrics:
On this glad day the glorious Sun
Of Righteousness arose;
On my benighted soul He shone
And filled it with repose.

parts.label: Verse 10
parts.lyrics:
Sudden expired the legal strife,
'Twas then I ceased to grieve;
My second, real, living life
I then began to live.

parts.label: Verse 11
parts.lyrics:
Then with my heart I first believed,
Believed with faith divine,
Power with the Holy Ghost received
To call the Savior mine.

parts.label: Verse 12
parts.lyrics:
I felt my Lord's atoning blood
Close to my soul applied;
Me, me He loved, the Son of God,
For me, for me He died!

parts.label: Verse 13
parts.lyrics:
I found and owned His promise true,
Ascertained of my part,
My pardon passed in heaven I knew
When written on my heart.

parts.label: Verse 14
parts.lyrics:
Look unto Him, ye nations, own
Your God, ye fallen race;
Look, and be saved through faith alone,
Be justified by grace.

parts.label: Verse 15
parts.lyrics:
See all your sins on Jesus laid:
The Lamb of God was slain,
His soul was once an offering made
For every soul of man.

parts.label: Verse 16
parts.lyrics:
Awake from guilty nature's sleep,
And Christ shall give you light,
Cast all your sins into the deep,
And wash the Æthiop white.

parts.label: Verse 17
parts.lyrics:
Harlots and publicans and thieves
In holy triumph join!
Saved is the sinner that believes
From crimes as great as mine.

parts.label: Verse 18
parts.lyrics:
Murderers and all ye hellish crew,
Ye sons of lust and pride,
Believe the Savior died for you;
For me the Savior died.

parts.label: Verse 19
parts.lyrics:
With me, your chief, ye then shall know,
Shall feel your sins forgiven;
Anticipate your heaven below,
And own that love is heaven.

hymns.title: O Holy Spirit, Enter In
hymns.words: Michael Schirmer, 1650 except verse 2 by unknown author circa 1660.
hymns.music: 'Wie Schön Leuchtet' Phillipp Nicolai, 1599.  Setting: "Mehrstimmiges ChoralBuch", 1906.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
O Holy Spirit, enter in,
And in our hearts Thy work begin
Thy Temple deign to make us;
Sun of the soul, Thou Light divine,
Around and in us brightly shine,
To joy and gladness wake us.
That we to Thee
Truly living, To Thee giving
Prayer unceasing
May in love be still increasing.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
Give to Thy Word impressive pow'r
That in our hearts, from this good hour,
As fire it may be glowing;
That we confess the Father, Son,
And Thee, the Spirit, Three in One,
Thy glory ever showing.
Stay Thou, guide now
Our souls ever that they never
May forsake Thee.
But by faith their refuge make Thee.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
Thou fountain whence all wisdom flows
Which God on pious hearts bestows,
Grant us Thy consolation.
That in our pure faith's unity
We faithful witnesses may be
Of grace that brings salvation.
Hear us, cheer us,
By Thy teaching; let our preaching,
And our labor
Praise Thee, Lord, and serve our neighbor.

parts.label: Verse 4
Verse 5
parts.lyrics:
Thy heav'nly strength sustain our heart
That we may act the valiant part
With Thee as our Reliance;
Be Thou our Refuge and our Shield
That we may never quit the field,
But stand in bold defiance.
Descend, defend
From all errors And earth's terrors
Thy salvation
Be our constant consolation.

parts.label: Verse 6
parts.lyrics:
O mighty Rock, O Source of life,
Let Thy dear Word 'mid doubt and strife
Be so within us burning,
That we be faithful unto death,
In Thy pure love and holy faith,
From Thee true wisdom learning!
Thy grace And peace
On us shower; By Thy power
Christ confessing,
Let us win our Savior's blessing.

parts.label: Verse 7
parts.lyrics:
O gentle Dew, from Heav'n now fall
With pow'r upon the hearts of all,
Thy tender love instilling,
That heart to heart more closely bound,
Fruitful in kindly deeds be found,
The law of love fulfilling;
The Lord, Discord
Shall not grieve Thee; We recieve Thee;
Where Thou livest.
Peace, and love, and joy Thou givest.

parts.label: Verse 8
parts.lyrics:
Grant that our days, while life shall last,
In purest holiness be passed,
Be Thou our Strength forever;
Grant that our hearts henceforth be free
From sinful lust and vanity
Which us from Thee must sever.
Keep Thou pure Now
From offenses Heart and senses.
Blessed Spirit!
Let us heavenly life inherit.

hymns.title: O Holy, Blessed Trinity
hymns.words: Martin Behm, 1608.  Translated by C. H. L. Schuette, 1880.
hymns.music: 'O Heilige Dreifaltigkeit' or 'Steht Auf, Ihr Lieben Kinderlein' Nikolaus Hermann, 1558.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
O Holy, Blessed Trinity,
Divine, Essential Unity,
God Father, Son, and Holy Ghost,
Be Thou this day my Guide and Host.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
My soul and body keep from harm,
O'er all I have extend Thine arm,
That Satan may not cause distress
Nor bring me shame or wretchedness.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
The Father's might shield me this day,
The Son's pure wisdom cheer my way,
The Holy Spirit's light divine
Illume my heart's benighted shrine.

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
My Maker, strengthen Thou my heart,
O my Redeemer, help impart,
Blest Comforter, keep at my side
That faith and love in me abide.

parts.label: Verse 5

hymns.title: O Little Town of Bethlehem
hymns.music: 'St. Louis' Lewis H. Redner, 1868.  Setting: "The Chapel Hymnal", 1898.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
O little town of Bethlehem,
how still we see thee lie!
Above thy deep and dreamless sleep
the silent stars go by.
Yet in thy dark streets shineth
the everlasting Light;
The hopes and fears of all the years
are met in thee tonight.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
For Christ is born of Mary,
and gathered all above,
While mortals sleep, the angels keep
their watch of wond'ring love.
O morning stars together,
proclaim the holy birth,
And praises sing to God the King,
and peace to men on earth!

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
How silently, how silently,
the wondrous Gift is giv'n;
So God imparts to human hearts
the blessings of His Heav'n.
No ear may hear His coming,
but in this world of sin,
Where meek souls will receive Him still,
the dear Christ enters in.

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
Where children pure and happy pray
to the blessèd Child,
Where misery cries out to Thee,
Son of the mother mild;
Where charity stands watching
and faith holds wide the door,
The dark night wakes, the glory breaks,
and Christmas comes once more.

parts.label: Verse 5
parts.lyrics:
O holy Child of Bethlehem,
descend to us, we pray;
Cast out our sin, and enter in,
be born in us today.
We hear the Christmas angels
the great glad tidings tell;
O come to us, abide with us,
our Lord Emmanuel!

hymns.title: O Lord My Soul Convicted
hymns.music: 'Winchester New' from "Musikalisches Handbuch", Hamburg, 1690.  Setting: Charles Lewis Hutchins, 1896.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
O Lord, my soul convicted stands
Of breaking all Thy ten commands:
And on me justly might'st Thou pour
Thy wrath in one eternal show'r.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
But thanks to God, its loud alarms
Have warn'd me of approaching harms;
And now, O Lord, my wants I see,
Lost and undone, I come to Thee.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
I know my fig leaf righteousness
Can ne'er Thy broken law redress;
Yet in the gospel plan I see,
There's hope of pardon e'en for me.

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
There, I behold with wonder, Lord!
That Christ hath to Thy law restor'd
Those honors on th'atoning day,
Which guilty sinners took away.

parts.label: Verse 5
parts.lyrics:
Amazing wisdom, pow'r and love,
Display'd to rebels from above!
Do Thou, O Lord, my faith increase
To love and trust Thy plan of grace.

hymns.title: O Lord of Heav'n and Earth and Sea
hymns.music: 'Es Ist Kein Tag' Johann D. Meyer, 1692.  Setting: "The English Hymnal", 1906.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
O Lord of Heav'n and earth and sea,
To Thee all praise and glory be;
How shall we show our love to Thee,
Who givest all?

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
The golden sunshine, vernal air,
Sweet flow'rs and fruits, Thy love declare;
Where harvests ripen, Thou art there,
Who givest all.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
For peaceful homes and healthful days,
For all the blessings earth displays,
We owe Thee thankfulness and praise,
Who givest all.

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
Thou didst not spare Thine only Son,
But gav'st Him for a world undone,
And freely, with that blessèd One,
Thou givest all.

parts.label: Verse 5
parts.lyrics:
Thou giv'st the Spirit's blessèd dow'r,
Spirit of life and love and pow'r,
And dost His sev'nfold graces show'r
Upon us all.

parts.label: Verse 6
parts.lyrics:
For souls redeemed, for sins forgiv'n,
For means of grace and hopes of Heav'n,
Father, all praise to Thee be giv'n,
Who givest all.

parts.label: Verse 7
parts.lyrics:
We lose what on ourselves we spend,
We have as treasure without end
Whatever, Lord, to Thee we lend,
Who givest all.

parts.label: Verse 8
parts.lyrics:
To Thee, from Whom we all derive
Our life, our gifts, our power to give:
O may we ever with Thee live,
Who givest all.

hymns.title: O Lord We Praise Thee
hymns.music: 'Gott Sei Gelobet und Gebenedeiet' or 'Enchiridion' or 'Gud Være Lovet Evig Nu'

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
O Lord, we praise Thee, bless Thee, and adore Thee,
In thanksgiving bow before Thee
Thou with Thy body and Thy blood didst nourish
Our weak souls that they may flourish:
O Lord, have mercy!
May Thy body, Lord, born of Mary,
That our sins and sorrows did carry,
And Thy blood for us plead
In all trial, fear, and need:
O Lord, have mercy!

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
Thy holy body into death was given,
Life to win for us in heaven.
No greater love than this to Thee could bind us;
May this feast thereof remind us!
O Lord, have mercy!
Lord, Thy kindness did so constrain Thee
That Thy blood should bless and sustain me.
All our debt Thou hast paid;
Peace with God once more is made:
O Lord, have mercy.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
May God bestow on us His grace and favor
To please Him with our behavior
And live as brethren here in love and union
Nor repent this blest Communion!
O Lord, have mercy!
Let not Thy good Spirit forsake us;
Grant that heav'nly- minded He make us;
Give Thy Church, Lord, to see
Days of peace and unity:
O Lord, have mercy!

hymns.title: O Lord, How Shall I Meet Thee
hymns.music: 'Wie Soll ich Dich Empfange' Johann Crüger, 1653.
topics: God's Children - the Faithful (see also Saints, People of the World)

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
O Lord, how shall I meet Thee,
How welcome Thee aright?
All nations long to see Thee,
My Hope, my heart's Delight!
O kindle, Lord, most holy,
Thy lamp within my breast,
To do in spirit lowly
All that may please Thee best.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
Thy Zion palms is strewing,
And branches fresh and fair;
My heart, its pow'rs renewing,
An anthem shall prepare.
My soul puts off her sadness
Thy glories to proclaim;
With all her strength and gladness
She fain would serve Thy Name.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
What hast Thou left ungranted
To give me glad relief?
When soul and body panted
In utmost depth of grief,
In deepest degradation,
Devoid of joy and peace,
Then, Thou, my soul's Salvation,
Didst come to bring release.

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
I lay in fetters groaning,
Thou com'st to set me free;
I stood, my shame bemoaning,
Thou com'st to honor me.
A glory Thou dost give me,
A treasure safe on high,
That will not fail nor leave me
As earthly riches fly.

parts.label: Verse 5
parts.lyrics:
Love caused Thine incarnation
Love brought Thee down to me;
Thy thirst for my salvation
Procured my liberty.
O love beyond all telling,
That led Thee to embrace,
In love all love excelling,
Our lost and fallen race!

hymns.title: O Lord, I Am Not Worthy
hymns.words: from Landshuter Gesangbuch, 1777. Translation unknown, before 1913.
hymns.music: 'Non Dignus' traditional air, before 1871.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
O Lord, I am not worthy
That Thou should'st come to me,
But speak the words of comfort,
My spirit healed shall be.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
O Lord, Thou art all holy,
The angels Thee adore;
How, then, ought I sincerely
My wrongs and sins deplore!

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
But when Thou soon wilt enter
My heart, my sinful heart,
Then heal me, be my shelter,
For Thou my Savior art.

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
O Lord, how can I thank Thee
For such a gift as this?
A gift which truly filleth
My soul with heav'nly bliss!

parts.label: Verse 5
parts.lyrics:
I praise Thee, I extol Thee,
I love Thee O my Sire,
Till once in joy and glory,
In heav'n I Thee admire.

hymns.title: O Love, How Deep, How Broad, How High
hymns.words: Unknown, 15th Century; Translated by Benjamin Webb, 1852, alt.
hymns.music: 'Deo Gracias' or 'Agincourt' traditional English, circa 1415.  Setting: Charles Winfred Douglas, 1918, alt.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
O love, how deep, how broad, how high,
How passing thought and fantasy,
That God, the Son of God, should take
Our mortal form for mortals' sake!

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
He sent no angel to our race
Of higher or of lower place,
But wore the robe of human frame
And He Himself, to this world came.

parts.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
For us baptized, for us He bore
His holy fast and hungered sore,
For us temptations sharp He knew;
For us the tempter overthrew.

parts.label: Verse 5
Verse 6
parts.lyrics:
For us to wicked men betrayed,
Scourged, mocked, in crown of thorns arrayed,
For us He bore the cross's death,
For us at length gave up His breath.

parts.label: Verse 7
Verse 8
parts.lyrics:
All honor, laud, and glory be,
O Jesus, virgin-born to Thee!
All glory, as is ever meet
To Father and to Paraclete.

hymns.title: O Sacred Head, Now Wounded
hymns.words: Bernard of Clairvaux, 1153. Translated by James W. Alexander, 1830.
hymns.music: 'Passion Chorale' or 'Herzlich Tut Mich Verlangen' Hans Leo Hassler, 1601. Adapted by J.S. Bach, 1729.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
O sacred Head, now wounded,
with grief and shame weighed down,
Now scornfully surrounded
with thorns, Thine only crown;
O sacred Head, what glory,
what bliss till now was Thine!
Yet, though despised and gory,
I joy to call Thee mine.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
What Thou, my Lord, hast suffered,
was all for sinners' gain;
Mine, mine was the transgression,
but Thine the deadly pain.
Lo, here I fall, my Savior!
'Tis I deserve Thy place;
Look on me with Thy favor,
vouchsafe to me Thy grace.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
Men mock and taunt and jeer Thee,
Thou noble countenance,
Though mighty worlds shall fear Thee
and flee before Thy glance.
How art thou pale with anguish,
with sore abuse and scorn!
How doth Thy visage languish
that once was bright as morn!

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
Now from Thy cheeks has vanished
their color once so fair;
From Thy red lips is banished
the splendor that was there.
Grim death, with cruel rigor,
hath robbed Thee of Thy life;
Thus Thou hast lost Thy vigor,
Thy strength in this sad strife.

parts.label: Verse 5
parts.lyrics:
My burden in Thy Passion,
Lord, Thou hast borne for me,
For it was my transgression
which brought this woe on Thee.
I cast me down before Thee,
wrath were my rightful lot;
Have mercy, I implore Thee;
Redeemer, spurn me not!

parts.label: Verse 6
parts.lyrics:
What language shall I borrow to thank Thee, dearest friend,
For this Thy dying sorrow, Thy pity without end?
O make me Thine forever, and should I fainting be,
Lord, let me never, never outlive my love to Thee.

parts.label: Verse 7
parts.lyrics:
My Shepherd, now receive me; my Guardian, own me Thine.
Great blessings Thou didst give me, O source of gifts divine.
Thy lips have often fed me with words of truth and love;
Thy Spirit oft hath led me to heavenly joys above.

parts.label: Verse 8
parts.lyrics:
Here I will stand beside Thee, from Thee I will not part;
O Savior, do not chide me! When breaks Thy loving heart,
When soul and body languish in death's cold, cruel grasp,
Then, in Thy deepest anguish, Thee in mine arms I'll clasp.

parts.label: Verse 9
parts.lyrics:
The joy can never be spoken, above all joys beside,
When in Thy body broken I thus with safety hide.
O Lord of Life, desiring Thy glory now to see,
Beside Thy cross expiring, I'd breathe my soul to Thee.

parts.label: Verse 10
parts.lyrics:
My Savior, be Thou near me when death is at my door;
Then let Thy presence cheer me, forsake me nevermore!
When soul and body languish, oh, leave me not alone,
But take away mine anguish by virtue of Thine own!

parts.label: Verse 11
parts.lyrics:
Be Thou my consolation, my shield when I must die;
Remind me of Thy passion when my last hour draws nigh.
Mine eyes shall then behold Thee, upon Thy cross shall dwell,
My heart by faith enfolds Thee. Who dieth thus dies well.

hymns.title: O That The Lord Would Guide My Ways
hymns.music: 'Evan' or 'Eva' William H. Havergal, 1847.  Setting: Lowell Mason, 1850.
topics: Submission (see also Following Jesus, God - Providence of, Trust)

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
O that the Lord would guide my ways
To keep His statutes still!
O that my God would grant me grace
To know and do His will!

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
O send Thy Spirit down to write
Thy law upon my heart!
Nor let my tongue indulge deceit,
Nor act the liar's part.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
From vanity turn off mine eyes;
Let no corrupt design,
Nor covetous desires arise
Within this soul of mine.

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
Order my footsteps by Thy Word,
And make my heart sincere;
Let sin have no dominion, Lord,
But keep my conscience clear.

parts.label: Verse 5
parts.lyrics:
Assist my soul, too apt to stray,
A stricter watch to keep;
And should I e'er forget Thy way,
Restore Thy wand'ring sheep.

parts.label: Verse 6
parts.lyrics:
Make me to walk in Thy commands, 'Tis a delightful road;
Nor let my head, or heart, or hands, Offend against my God.

hymns.title: O The Deep, Deep Love of Jesus
hymns.music: 'Ebenezer' or 'Ton-Y-Botel' Thomas J. Williams, 1890.  Setting: "A Hymnal" (Episcopal), 1916.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
O the deep, deep love of Jesus,
vast, unmeasured, boundless, free!
Rolling as a mighty ocean
in its fullness over me!
Underneath me, all around me,
is the current of Thy love
Leading onward, leading homeward
to Thy glorious rest above!

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
O the deep, deep love of Jesus,
spread His praise from shore to shore!
How He loveth, ever loveth,
changeth never, nevermore!
How He watches o'er His loved ones,
died to call them all His own;
How for them He intercedeth,
watcheth o'er them from the throne!

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
O the deep, deep love of Jesus,
love of every love the best!
'Tis an ocean full of blessing,
'tis a haven giving rest!
O the deep, deep love of Jesus,
'tis a heav'n of heav'ns to me;
And it lifts me up to glory,
for it lifts me up to Thee!

hymns.title: O Trinity of Blessed Light
hymns.words: Ambrose of Milan, 4th Century.  German version by M. Luther, 1543.
hymns.music: 'O Lux Beata Trinitas' ancient Latin.  Setting: "A Hymnal" (Episcopal), 1916.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
O Trinity of blessèd light,
