O Unity of princely might,
The fiery sun now goes his way;
Shed Thou within our hearts a ray.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
To Thee our morning song of praise,
To Thee our evening prayer we raise;
O grant us with Thy saints on high
To praise Thee through eternity.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
All laud to God the Father be,
All praise, eternal Son, to Thee,
All glory, as is ever meet,
To God the holy Paraclete.

hymns.title: O Wondrous Type, O Vision Fair
hymns.words: From the "Sarum Breviary", 1495.  Translated by John Mason Neale, 1851.
hymns.music: 'Deo Gracias' or 'Agincourt' traditional English, circa 1415.  Setting: Charles Winfred Douglas, 1918, alt.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
O wondrous type! O vision fair
Of glory that the Church may share,
Which Christ upon the mountain shows,
where brighter than the sun He glows!

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
From age to age the tale declare,
How with the three disciples there,
Where Moses and Elijah meet,
The Lord holds converse high and sweet.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
The law and prophets there have place,
Two chosen witnesses of grace;
The Father's voice from out the cloud
proclaims His only Son aloud.

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
With shining face and bright array,
Christ deigns to manifest today
What glory shall be theirs above
who joy in God with perfect love.

parts.label: Verse 5
parts.lyrics:
And faithful hearts are raised on high
by this great vision's mystery;
For which in joyful strains we raise
the voice of prayer, the hymn of praise.

parts.label: Verse 6
parts.lyrics:
O Father, with th'Eternal Son,
and Holy Spirit, ever One,
Vouchsafe to bring us by Thy grace
to see Thy glory face to face.

hymns.title: Of The Father's Love Begotten
hymns.music: 'Divinum Mysterium' or 'Corde Natus' Latin Plainsong, 13th Century.
topics: Adam (first/second - see also Guidance, Invitation [ours to God], Repentance) [3]
Children (see also God's Children - the Faithful) [8]
God's Children - the Faithful (see also Saints, People of the World) [5,8]

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
Of the Father's love begotten
Ere the worlds began to be,
He is Alpha and Omega,
He the source, the ending He,
Of the things that are, that have been,
And that future years shall see,
Evermore and evermore!

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
At His Word they were created;
He commanded; it was done:
Heav'n and earth and depths of ocean
In their threefold order one;
All that grows beneath the shining
Of the moon and burning sun,
Evermore and evermore!

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
He is found in human fashion,
Death and sorrow here to know,
That the race of Adam's children,
Doomed by law to endless woe,
May not henceforth die and perish
In the dreadful gulf below,
Evermore and evermore!

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
Oh that birth forever blessèd!
When the virgin, full of grace,
By the Holy Ghost conceiving,
Bare the Savior of our race;
And the Babe, the world's Redeemer,
First revealed His sacred face,
Evermore and evermore!

parts.label: Verse 5
parts.lyrics:
O ye heights of heav'n adore Him;
Angel hosts, His praises sing;
Pow'rs, dominions, bow before Him,
and extol our God and King:
Let no tongue on earth be silent,
Every voice in concert ring,
Evermore and evermore!

parts.label: Verse 6
parts.lyrics:
He is here, Whom seers in old time Chanted of, while ages ran;
Whom the writings of the prophets Promised since the world began:
Then foretold, now manifested, to receive the praise of man,
Evermore and evermore!

parts.label: Verse 7
parts.lyrics:
Righteous Judge of souls departed, Righteous King of them that live,
On the Father's throne exalted None in might with Thee may strive;
Who at last in vengeance coming Sinners from Thy face shalt drive,
Evermore and evermore!

parts.label: Verse 8
parts.lyrics:
Thee let old men, Thee let young men, Thee let choirs of infants sing;
Thee the matrons and the virgins, And the children answering:
Let their guileless songs re-echo, And the heart its music bring,
Evermore and evermore!

parts.label: Verse 9
parts.lyrics:
Christ, to Thee with God the Father, And, O Holy Ghost, to Thee,
Hymn and chant with high thanksgiving, And unwearied praises be:
Honor, glory, and dominion, And eternal victory,
Evermore and evermore!

hymns.title: Oh, Blest the House
hymns.words: Christoph C. L. von Pfeil, 1735. Translated by Catherine Winkworth, 1863, alt.
hymns.music: 'Wo Gott Zum Haus' from Klug's Geistliche Lieder, 1533.
topics: Children (see also God's Children - the Faithful) [5]

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
Oh blest the house, whate'er befall,
Where Jesus Christ is All in All;
Yea, if He were not dwelling there,
How poor and dark and void it were!

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
Oh blest that house where faith ye find,
And all within have set their mind
To trust their God and serve Him still,
And do in all His holy will.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
Blest, where their prayers shall daily rise
As fragrant incense to the skies,
While in their lives the world is taught
That forms without the heart are naught.

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
Blest, where the busy hands fulfil
Their proper task with ready skill,
While through their different works ye see
One spirit run of unity.

parts.label: Verse 5
parts.lyrics:
Blest such a house, it prospers well,
In peace and joy the parents dwell,
And in their children's lot is shown
How richly God can bless His own.

parts.label: Verse 6
parts.lyrics:
Then here will I and mine to-day
A solemn covenant make, and say,--
Though all the world forsake Thy Word,
I and my house will serve the Lord.

hymns.title: On Jordan's Bank the Baptist's Cry
hymns.words: Charles Coffin, 1736. st. 1-3 translated by John Chandler, 1837; st 4-5 translator unknown.
hymns.music: 'Puer Nobis Nascitur' Michael Praetorius, 1609.
topics: Submission (see also Following Jesus, God - Providence of, Trust)

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
On Jordan's bank the Baptist's cry
Announces that the Lord is nigh;
Come, then, and hearken, for he brings
Glad tidings from the King of kings!

parts.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
For Thou art our Salvation, Lord,
Our Refuge, and our great Reward.
Without Thy grace our souls must fade
And wither like a flow'r decayed.

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
Stretch forth Thine hand, to heal our sore,
And make us rise and fall no more;
Once more upon Thy people shine,
And fill the world with love divine.

parts.label: Verse 5
parts.lyrics:
To Him Who left the throne of Heav'n
To save mankind, all praise be giv'n;
Like praise be to the Father done,
And Holy Spirit, Three in One.

hymns.title: On What Has Now Been Sown
hymns.music: 'Darwall`s 148th' John Darwall, 1770.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
On what has now been sown
Thy blessing, Lord, bestow;
The pow'r is Thine alone
To make it spring and grow.
Do Thou in grace the harvest raise,
And Thou alone shalt have the praise.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
To Thee our wants are known,
From Thee are all our pow'rs;
Accept what is Thine own
And pardon what is ours.
Our praises, Lord, and prayers receive
And to Thy Word a blessing give.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
Oh, grant that each of us
Now met before Thee here
May meet together thus
When Thou and Thine appear
And follow Thee to Heav'n, our home.
E'en so, Amen, Lord Jesus, come!

hymns.title: One Thing's Needful
hymns.words: Johann H. Schröder, 1697.  Translated by Frances E. Cox, 1841, alt.
hymns.music: 'Eins ist Not' Adam Krieger (1634-1666).  Setting: Fridrich Layriz, 1853, alt.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
One thing's needful: then, Lord Jesus,
Keep this one thing in my mind;
All beside, though first it please us,
Soon a grievous yoke we find:
Beneath it the heart is still fretting and striving,
No true, lasting happiness ever deriving.
The gain of this one thing all loss can requite
And teach me in all things to find true delight.

parts.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
How were Mary's thoughts devoted,
Her eternal joy to find,
As intent each word she noted,
At her Savior's feet reclined:
How kindled her heart, how devout was its feeling,
While hearing the lessons that Christ was revealing;
For Jesus all earthly concerns she forgot,
And all was repaid in that one happy lot.

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
Thus my longings, heav'nward tending,
Jesus, rest alone on Thee;
Help me, thus on Thee depending,
Savior! come and dwell in me:
Although all the world should forsake and forget Thee,
In love I will follow Thee, ne'er will I quit Thee;
For Jesus, both Spirit and life is Thy Word,
And is there a joy which Thou dost not afford?

parts.label: Verse 5
parts.lyrics:
Wisdom's highest noblest treasure,
Jesus, lies conceal'd in Thee;
Grant that this may still the measure
Of my will and actions be:
Humility there and simplicity reigning,
My steps shall in wisdom for ever be training;
Oh! if I of Christ have this knowledge divine,
The fullness of heavenly wisdom is mine.

parts.label: Verse 6
parts.lyrics:
Christ, Thou art the sole oblation
That I'll bring before my God;
In his sight I've acceptation
Only through Thy streaming blood:
Immaculate righteousness now I've acquired,
Since Thou on the tree of the cross hast expired;
The robe of salvation for ever is mine,
In this shall my faith through eternity shine.

parts.label: Verse 7
parts.lyrics:
Let my soul, in full exemption,
Wake up in Thy likeness now;
Thou art made to me redemption,
My sanctification Thou.
Whatever I need for my Journey to Heaven
In Thee, I my Savior, is unto me given.
Oh! let me all perishing pleasures forgo,
And Thy life, O Jesus! alone let me know.

parts.label: Verse 8
parts.lyrics:
Where should else my hopes be centered?
Grace o'erwhelms me with its flood;
Thou, my Savior, once hast enter'd
Holiest heaven through Thy blood:
Eternal redemption for sinners there finding,
From hell's dark dominion my spirit unbinding,
To me perfect freedom Thy entrance has brought,
And childlike to cry, "Abba, Father," I'm taught.

parts.label: Verse 9
parts.lyrics:
Christ Himself, my Shepherd, feeds me,
Peace and joy my spirit fill;
In a pasture green He leads me
Forth beside the waters still:
Oh! naught to my soul is so sweet and reviving,
As thus unto Jesus alone to be living;
True happiness this, and this only supplies,
Through faith on my Savior to fasten my eyes.

parts.label: Verse 10
parts.lyrics:
Therefore, Jesus, my Salvation,
Thou my One, my All shalt be;
Prove my fix'd determination,
Root out all hypocrisy:
Look well if on sin's slippery paths I am hasting,
And lead me, O Lord, in the way everlasting;
This one thing is needful, all others are vain,
I count all but loss that I Christ may obtain.

hymns.title: Open Now Thy Gates of Beauty
hymns.words: Benjamin Schmolck, 1730.  Translated by Catherine Winkworth, 1863.
hymns.music: 'Unser Herrscher' or 'Neander' Joachim Neander, 1680.  Setting: "Chorale Book for England", 1863.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
Open now thy gates of beauty,
Zion, let me enter there,
Where my soul in joyful duty
Waits for Him Who answers prayer.
Oh, how blessèd is this place,
Filled with solace, light and grace!

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
Lord, my God, I come before Thee,
Come Thou also unto me;
Where we find Thee and adore Thee,
There a heav'n on earth must be.
To my heart, oh, enter Thou,
Let it be Thy temple now!

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
Here Thy praise is gladly chanted,
Here Thy seed is duly sown;
Let my soul, where it is planted,
Bring forth precious sheaves alone,
So that all I hear may be
Fruitful unto life in me.

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
Thou my faith increase and quicken,
Let me keep Thy gift divine,
Howsoe'er temptations thicken;
May Thy Word still o'er me shine
As my guiding star through life,
As my comfort in my strife.

parts.label: Verse 5
parts.lyrics:
Speak, O God, and I will hear Thee,
Let Thy will be done indeed;
May I undisturbed draw near Thee
While Thou dost Thy people feed.
Here of life the fountain flows,
Here is balm for all our woes.

hymns.title: Our Father Thou in Heaven Above
hymns.music: 'Vater Unser im Himmelreich' attr. Martin Luther, found in Valentin Schumann's Geistliche Lieder, Leipzig, 1539.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
Our Father, Thou in heav'n above,
Who biddest us to dwell in love,
As brethren of one family,
To cry in ev'ry need to Thee,
Teach us no thoughtless word to say,
But from our inmost heart to pray.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
Thy name be hallowed. Help us, Lord,
In purity to keep Thy Word,
That to the glory of Thy Name
We walk before Thee free from blame.
Let no false doctrine us pervert;
All poor, deluded souls convert.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
Thy kingdom come. Thine let it be
In time and in eternity.
Let Thy good Spirit e'er be nigh
Our hearts with graces to supply.
Break Satan's pow'r, defeat his rage;
Preserve Thy Church from age to age.

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
Thy gracious will on earth be done
As 'tis in heav'n before Thy throne;
Obedience in our weal and woe
And patience in all grief bestow.
Curb flesh and blood and ev'ry ill
That sets itself against Thy will.

parts.label: Verse 5
parts.lyrics:
Give us this day our daily bread
And let us all be clothed and fed.
From war and strife be our Defense,
From famine and from pestilence,
That we may live in godly peace,
Free from all care and avarice.

parts.label: Verse 6
parts.lyrics:
Forgive our sins, Lord, we implore,
Remove from us their burden sore,
As we their trespasses forgive
Who by offenses us do grieve.
Thus let us dwell in charity
And serve our brother willingly.

parts.label: Verse 7
parts.lyrics:
Into temptation lead us not.
When evil foes against us plot
And vex our souls on every hand,
Oh, give us strength that we may stand
Firm in the faith, a well-armed host,
Through comfort of the Holy Ghost!

parts.label: Verse 8
parts.lyrics:
From evil, Lord, deliver us;
The times and days are perilous.
Redeem us from eternal death,
And when we yield our dying breath,
Console us, grant us calm release,
And take our souls to Thee in peace.

parts.label: Verse 9
parts.lyrics:
Amen, that is, So shall it be.
Confirm our faith and hope in Thee
That we may doubt not, but believe
What here we ask we shall receive.
Thus in Thy name and at Thy word
We say: Amen. Oh, hear us, Lord! Amen.

hymns.title: Our God, Our Help In Ages Past
hymns.music: 'St. Anne' William Croft, 1708.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
Our God, our help in ages past,
Our hope for years to come,
Our shelter from the stormy blast,
And our eternal home.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
Under the shadow of Thy throne
Thy saints have dwelt secure;
Sufficient is Thine arm alone,
And our defense is sure.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
Before the hills in order stood,
Or earth received her frame,
From everlasting Thou art God,
To endless years the same.

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
Thy Word commands our flesh to dust,
'Return, ye sons of men:'
All nations rose from earth at first,
And turn to earth again.

parts.label: Verse 5
parts.lyrics:
A thousand ages in Thy sight
Are like an evening gone;
Short as the watch that ends the night
Before the rising sun.

parts.label: Verse 6
parts.lyrics:
The busy tribes of flesh and blood,
With all their lives and cares,
Are carried downwards by the flood,
And lost in following years.

parts.label: Verse 7
parts.lyrics:
Time, like an ever rolling stream,
Bears all its sons away;
They fly, forgotten, as a dream
Dies at the opening day.

parts.label: Verse 8
parts.lyrics:
Like flowery fields the nations stand
Pleased with the morning light;
The flowers beneath the mower's hand
Lie withering ere 'tis night.

parts.label: Verse 9
parts.lyrics:
Our God, our help in ages past,
Our hope for years to come,
Be Thou our guard while troubles last,
And our eternal home.

hymns.title: Out of the Deep I Cry to Thee (Aus Tiefer Not (Luther))
hymns.words: Martin Luther, 1524. Translated by Arthur Tozer Russell (1806-1874).
hymns.music: 'Aus Tiefer Not (Luther)' or 'Af Dybsens Nød' Martin Luther from Erfurt Enchiridion, 1524.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
Out of the deep I cry to Thee;
O Lord God, hear my crying:
Incline Thy gracious ear to me,
With prayer to Thee applying.
For if Thou fix Thy searching eye
On all sin and iniquity,
Who, Lord, can stand before Thee?

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
But love and grace with Thee prevail,
O God, our sins forgiving;
The holiest deeds can naught avail
Of all before Thee living.
Before Thee none can boast him clear;
Therefore must each Thy judgment fear,
And live on Thy compassion.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
For this, my hope in God shall rest,
Naught building on my merit;
My heart confides, of Him possest,
His goodness stays my spirit.
His precious word assureth me;
My solace, my sure Rock is he,
Whereon my soul abideth.

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
And though I wait the livelong night
And till the morn returneth,
My heart undoubting trusts His might
Nor in impatience mourneth.
Born of His Spirit, Israel
In the right Way thus fareth well,
And on his God reposeth

parts.label: Verse 5
parts.lyrics:
What though our sins are manifold?
Supreme His mercy reigneth;
No limit can His hand withhold,
Where evil most obtaineth.
He the good Shepherd is alone,
Who Israel will redeem and own,
Forgiving all transgression.

hymns.title: Out of the Deep I Cry to Thee (Aus Tiefer Not (Strassburg))
hymns.words: Martin Luther, 1524. Translated by Arthur Tozer Russell (1806-1874).
hymns.music: 'Aus Tiefer Not (Strassburg)' or 'Strassburg' from Köpfel's Gesangbuch, Strassburg, 1525.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
Out of the deep I cry to Thee;
O Lord God, hear my crying:
Incline Thy gracious ear to me,
With prayer to Thee applying.
For if Thou fix Thy searching eye
On all sin and iniquity,
Who, Lord, can stand before Thee?

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
But love and grace with Thee prevail,
O God, our sins forgiving;
The holiest deeds can naught avail
Of all before Thee living.
Before Thee none can boast him clear;
Therefore must each Thy judgment fear,
And live on Thy compassion.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
For this, my hope in God shall rest,
Naught building on my merit;
My heart confides, of Him possest,
His goodness stays my spirit.
His precious word assureth me;
My solace, my sure Rock is He,
Whereon my soul abideth.

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
And though I wait the livelong night
And till the morn returneth,
My heart undoubting trusts His might
Nor in impatience mourneth.
Born of His Spirit, Israel
In the right Way thus fareth well,
And on his God reposeth

parts.label: Verse 5
parts.lyrics:
What though our sins are manifold?
Supreme His mercy reigneth;
No limit can His hand withhold,
Where evil most obtaineth.
He the good Shepherd is alone,
Who Israel will redeem and own,
Forgiving all transgression.

hymns.title: Over Kidron Jesus Treadeth
hymns.words: Thomas Hansen Kingo, 1689.  Translated by J. Jeffrey, before 1866.
hymns.music: 'Over Kedron Jesus Traeder' Ludvig Mathias Lindeman.  Setting: "The Lutheran Hymnary", 1913.
topics: Submission (see also Following Jesus, God - Providence of, Trust)

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
Over Kidron Jesus treadeth
To His passion for us all;
Every human eye be weeping,
Tears of bitter grief let fall!
Round His Spirit flock the foes,
Place their shafts and bend their bows,
Aiming at the Savior solely,
While the world forsakes Him wholly.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
David once, with heart afflicted,
Crossed the Kidron's narrow strand,
Clouds of gloom and grief about him
When an exile from his land.
But, O Jesus, blacker now
Bends the cloud above Thy brow,
Hasting to death's dreary portals
For the shame and sin of mortals.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
See how, anguish struck, He falleth
Prostrate, and with struggling breath,
Three times on His God He calleth,
Praying that the bitter death
And the cup of doom may go,
Still He cries, in all His woe:
"Not My will, but Thine, O Father!"
And the angels round Him gather.

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
See how, in that hour of darkness,
Battling with the evil pow'r,
Agonies untold assail Him,
On His soul the arrows show'r;
All the garden flow'rs are wet
With the drops of bloody sweat,
From His anguished frame distilling-
World's redemption thus fulfilling!

parts.label: Verse 5
parts.lyrics:
But, O flow'rs, so sadly watered
By this pure and precious dew,
In some blessed hour your blossoms
'Neath the olive shadows grew!
Eden's garden did not bear
Aught that can with you compare,
For the blood, thus freely given,
Makes my soul the heir of heaven.

parts.label: Verse 6
parts.lyrics:
When as flow'rs themselves I wither, When I droop and fade like grass,
When the life-streams through my pulses Dull and ever duller pass,
When at last they cease to roll, Then, to cheer my sinking soul,
Grace of Jesus, be Thou given- Source of triumph! pledge of heaven!

hymns.title: Pass Me Not, O Gentle Savior
hymns.tune: Pass Me Not O Gentle Savior
hymns.music: 'Pass Me Not O Gentle Savior' William Howard Doane, 1870.  Setting: "The Coronation", 1872.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
Pass me not, O gentle Savior,
Hear my humble cry;
While on others Thou art calling,
Do not pass me by.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
Let me at Thy throne of mercy
Find a sweet relief,
Kneeling there in deep contrition;
Help my unbelief.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
3, Trusting only in Thy merit,
Would I seek Thy face;
Heal my wounded, broken spirit,
Save me by Thy grace.

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
Thou the Spring of all my comfort,
More than life to me, Whom have I on earth beside Thee? Whom in
Heav'n but Thee?

parts.label: Refrain

hymns.title: Praise God From Whom All Blessings Flow
hymns.music: 'Old 100th' Genevan Psalter, attr. Louis Bourgeois, c. 1551.

parts.label: Verse 1

hymns.title: Praise My Soul The King Of Heaven
hymns.music: 'Praise My Soul' or 'Lauda Anima' or 'St. Paul' John Goss, 1869.  Setting: "The Choral Hymnal", 1888.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
Praise, my soul, the King of heaven;
To His feet thy tribute bring.
Ransomed, healed, restored, forgiven,
Evermore His praises sing:
Alleluia! Alleluia!
Praise the everlasting King.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
Praise Him for His grace and favor
To our fathers in distress.
Praise Him still the same as ever,
Slow to chide, and swift to bless.
Alleluia! Alleluia!
Glorious in His faithfulness.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
Father like He tends and spares us;
Well our feeble frame He knows.
In His hands He gently bears us,
Rescues us from all our foes.
Alleluia! Alleluia!
Widely yet His mercy flows.

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
Frail as summer's flower we flourish,
Blows the wind and it is gone;
But while mortals rise and perish
Our God lives unchanging on,
Praise Him, Praise Him, Hallelujah
Praise the High Eternal One!

parts.label: Verse 5

hymns.title: Praise The Lord, Ye Heavens Adore Him
hymns.music: 'Austria (Haydn)' or 'Austrian Hymn' Franz Joseph Haydn, 1797.
topics: Submission (see also Following Jesus, God - Providence of, Trust)

parts.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
Worship, honor, glory, blessing,
Lord, we offer unto Thee.
Young and old, Thy praise expressing,
In glad homage bend the knee.
All the saints in Heav'n adore Thee;
We would bow before Thy throne.
As Thine angels serve before Thee,
So on earth Thy will be done.

hymns.title: Praise To The Lord, The Almighty
hymns.words: Joachim Neander, 1680. Translated by Catherine Winkworth, 1863.
hymns.music: 'Lobe den Herren' from Ander Theil des Erneuerten Gesangbuch, 1665.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
Praise to the Lord, the Almighty, the King of creation!
O my soul, praise Him, for He is thy health and salvation!
All ye who hear,
now to His temple draw near;
Praise Him in glad adoration.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
Praise to the Lord, Who o'er all things so wondrously reigneth,
Shelters thee under His wings, yea, so gently sustaineth!
Hast thou not seen
how thy desires have been
Granted in what He ordaineth

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
Praise to the Lord, Who hath fearfully, wondrously, made thee;
Health hath vouchsafed and, when heedlessly falling, hath stayed thee.
What need or grief
ever hath failed of relief?
Wings of His mercy did shade thee.

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
Praise to the Lord, Who doth prosper thy work and defend thee;
Surely His goodness and mercy here daily attend thee.
Ponder anew
what the Almighty can do,
If with His love He befriend thee.

parts.label: Verse 5
parts.lyrics:
Praise to the Lord, Who, when tempests their warfare are waging,
Who, when the elements madly around thee are raging,
Biddeth them cease,
turneth their fury to peace,
Whirlwinds and waters assuaging.

hymns.title: Rejoice, My Heart, Be Glad and Sing
hymns.music: 'Ich Singe dir mit Herz' Johann Balthasar König, 1738.
topics: Submission (see also Following Jesus, God - Providence of, Trust) [6]

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
Rejoice, my heart, be glad and sing,
A cheerful trust maintain;
For God, the Source of everything,
Thy Portion shall remain.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
He is thy Treasure, He thy Joy,
Thy Life and Light and Lord,
Thy Counselor when doubts annoy,
Thy Shield and great Reward.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
Why spend the day in blank despair,
In restless thought the night?
On thy Creator cast thy care;
He makes thy burdens light.

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
Did not His love and truth and pow'r
Watch o'er thy childhood day?
Has He not oft in threat'ning hour
Turned dreaded ills away?

parts.label: Verse 5
parts.lyrics:
His wisdom never plans in vain,
Ne'er falters or mistakes;
All that His counsels did ordain
A happy ending makes.

hymns.title: Rejoice, O Pilgrim Throng
hymns.music: 'Marion' Arthur H. Messiter, 1883.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
Rejoice, O pilgrim throng!
Rejoice, give thanks, and sing;
Your festal banner wave on high,
The cross of Christ your King.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
With all the angel choirs,
With all the saints on earth,
Pour out the strains of joy and bliss,
True rapture, noblest mirth.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
With voice as full and strong
As ocean's surging praise,
Send forth the hymns our fathers loved,
The psalms of ancient days.

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
Still lift your standard high,
Still march in firm array,
As warriors through the darkness toil,
Till dawns the golden day.

parts.label: Verse 5
parts.lyrics:
Yes, on through life's long path,
Still chanting as ye go;
From youth to age, by night and day,
In gladness and in woe.

parts.label: Verse 6
parts.lyrics:
Yes onward, onward still With hymn, and chant and song,
Through gate, and porch and columned aisle, The hallowed pathways throng.

parts.label: Verse 7
parts.lyrics:
At last the march shall end; The wearied ones shall rest;
The pilgrims find their Father's house, Jerusalem the bless'd.

parts.label: Verse 8
parts.lyrics:
Then on, ye pure in heart! Rejoice, give thanks and sing!
Your festal banner wave on high, The cross of Christ your King.

parts.label: Refrain
parts.lyrics:
Rejoice, rejoice, rejoice,
Give thanks and sing.

hymns.title: Rescue the Perishing
hymns.music: 'Rescue the Perishing' William Howard Doane, 1870.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
Rescue the perishing, care for the dying,
Snatch them in pity from sin and the grave;
Weep o'er the erring one, lift up the fallen,
Tell them of Jesus, the mighty to save.

parts.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
Down in the human heart, crushed by the tempter,
Feelings lie buried that grace can restore;
Touched by a loving heart, wakened by kindness,
Chords that were broken will vibrate once more.

parts.label: Verse 4
Refrain
parts.lyrics: Rescue the perishing, care for the dying, Jesus is merciful, Jesus will save.

hymns.title: Rock of Ages
hymns.music: 'Toplady' Thomas Hastings, 1830.

parts.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
Verse 3
Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
While I draw this fleeting breath,
When mine eyes shall close in death,
When I soar to worlds unknown,
See Thee on Thy judgment throne,
Rock of Ages, cleft for me,
Let me hide myself in Thee.

hymns.title: Salvation Unto Us Has Come
hymns.tune: Es ist das Heil uns Kommen Her
hymns.music: 'Es ist das Heil uns Kommen Her' traditional German circa 1400 from Etlich Christlich Lider, Wittenberg, 1524.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
Salvation unto us has come
By God's free grace and favor;
Good works cannot avert our doom,
They help and save us never.
Faith looks to Jesus Christ alone,
Who did for all the world atone;
He is our one Redeemer.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
What God did in His law demand
And none to Him could render
Caused wrath and woe on every hand
For man, the vile offender.
Our flesh has not those pure desires
The spirit of the Law requires,
And lost is our condition.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
It was a false, misleading dream
That God His Law had given
So sinners could themselves redeem
And by their works gain Heaven.
The Law is but a mirror bright
To bring the inbred sin to light
That lurks within our nature.

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
From sin our flesh could not abstain
Sin held its sway unceasing;
The task was useless and in vain,
Our guilt was e'er increasing.
None can remove sin's poisoned dart
Or purify our guileful heart?
So deep is our corruption.

hymns.title: Savior Of The Nations Come
hymns.words: Ambrose of Milan, c. 397.  Translated to German by Martin Luther, 1524.
hymns.music: 'Nun Komm, Der Heiden Heiland' from Walter's Geistliche Gesangbüchlein, 1524.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
Savior of the nations, come;
Virgin's Son, here make Thy home!
Marvel now, O heav'n and earth,
That the Lord chose such a birth.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
Not by human flesh and blood;
By the Spirit of our God
Was the Word of God made flesh,
Woman's offspring, pure and fresh.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
Wondrous birth! O wondrous Child
Of the virgin undefiled!
Though by all the world disowned,
Still to be in heaven enthroned.

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
From the Father forth He came
And returneth to the same,
Captive leading death and hell
High the song of triumph swell!

parts.label: Verse 5
parts.lyrics:
Thou, the Father's only Son,
Hast o'er sin the vict'ry won.
Boundless shall Thy kingdom be;
When shall we its glories see?

parts.label: Verse 6
parts.lyrics:
Brightly doth Thy manger shine,
Glorious is its light divine.
Let not sin o'ercloud this light;
Ever be our faith thus bright.

parts.label: Verse 7
parts.lyrics:
Praise to God the Father sing,
Praise to God the Son, our King,
Praise to God the Spirit be
Ever and eternally.

hymns.title: Savior When In Dust To Thee
hymns.music: 'Aberystwyth (Parry)' Joseph Parry, 1879.  Setting: "The English Hymnal", 1906.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
Savior, when in dust to Thee
Low we bow th'adoring knee,
When, repentant, to the skies
Scarce we lift our weeping eyes,
O by all the pains and woes
Suffered once for man below,
Bending from Thy throne on high,
Hear our penitential cry!

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
By Thy helpless infant years,
By Thy life of want and tears,
By Thy days of sore distress
In the savage wilderness,
By the dread mysterious hour
Of th'insulting tempter's pow'r,
Turn, O turn a fav'ring eye,
Hear our penitential cry!

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
By the sacred griefs that wept
O'er the grave where Laz'rus slept,
By the boding tears that flowed
Over Salem's loved abode,
By the anguished sigh that told
Treachery lurked within Thy fold,
From Thy seat above the sky,
Hear our penitential cry!

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
By Thine hour of dire despair,
By Thine agony of prayer,
By the cross, the nail, the thorn,
Piercing spear, and torturing scorn,
By the gloom that veiled the skies
O'er the dreadful sacrifice,
Listen to our humble cry,
Hear our penitential cry!

parts.label: Verse 5
parts.lyrics:
By Thy deep expiring groan,
By the sad sepulchral stone,
By the vault whose dark abode
Held in vain the rising God,
O from earth to heaven restored,
Mighty, reascended Lord,
Listen, listen to the sigh
Of our penitential cry!

hymns.title: Savior, Like A Shepherd Lead Us
hymns.music: 'Bradbury' William B. Bradbury, 1859.
topics: Submission (see also Following Jesus, God - Providence of, Trust)

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
Savior, like a shepherd lead us,
much we need Thy tender care;
In Thy pleasant pastures feed us,
for our use Thy folds prepare.
Blessèd Jesus, blessèd Jesus!
Thou hast bought us, Thine we are.
Blessèd Jesus, blessèd Jesus!
Thou hast bought us, Thine we are.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
We are Thine, Thou dost befriend us,
be the guardian of our way;
Keep Thy flock, from sin defend us,
seek us when we go astray.
Blessèd Jesus, blessèd Jesus!
Hear, O hear us when we pray.
Blessèd Jesus, blessèd Jesus!
Hear, O hear us when we pray.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
Thou hast promised to receive us,
poor and sinful though we be;
Thou hast mercy to relieve us,
grace to cleanse and pow'r to free.
Blessèd Jesus, blessèd Jesus!
We will early turn to Thee.
Blessèd Jesus, blessèd Jesus!
We will early turn to Thee.

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
Early let us seek Thy favor,
early let us do Thy will;
Blessèd Lord and only Savior,
with Thy love our bosoms fill.
Blessèd Jesus, blessèd Jesus!
Thou hast loved us, love us still.
Blessèd Jesus, blessèd Jesus!
Thou hast loved us, love us still.

hymns.title: Savior, Who Thy Flock Art Feeding
hymns.music: 'Batty' or 'Ringe recht' from Johann Thommen's Musicalischer Christenschatz, Basel, 1745.
topics: Children (see also God's Children - the Faithful)
God's Children - the Faithful (see also Saints, People of the World)

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
Savior, who Thy flock art feeding
With the Shepherd's kindest care,
All the feeble gently leading,
While the lambs Thy bosom share.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
Now, these little ones receiving,
Fold them in Thy gracious arm;
There, we know, Thy Word believing,
Only there secure from harm.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
Never, from Thy pasture roving,
Let them be the lion's prey;
Let Thy tenderness, so loving,
Keep them through life's dang'rous way.

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
Then within Thy fold eternal
Let them find a resting place,
Feed in pastures ever vernal,
Drink the rivers of Thy grace.

hymns.title: See Amid the Winter's Snow
hymns.music: 'Humility' John Goss, 1870.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
See amid the winter's snow,
Born for us on earth below,
See, the gentle Lamb appears,
Promised from eternal years.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
Lo, within a manger lies He Who built the starry skies; He Who, thronèd in height sublime,
Sits amid the cherubim.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
Say, you holy shepherds, say,
Tell your joyful news today.
Why have you now left your sheep
On the lonely mountain steep?

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
"As we watched at dead of night,
Lo, we saw a wondrous light;
Angels singing 'Peace on earth'
Told us of the
Savior's birth."

parts.label: Verse 5
parts.lyrics:
Sacred Infant, all divine,
What a tender love was Thine,
Thus to come from highest bliss
Down to such a world as this.

parts.label: Verse 6
parts.lyrics:
Teach, O teach us, holy Child,
By Thy face so meek and mild,
Teach us to resemble Thee,
In Thy sweet humility.

parts.label: Refrain
parts.lyrics:
Hail that ever blessèd morn,
Hail redemption's happy dawn,
Sing through all Jerusalem: Christ is born in Bethlehem.

hymns.title: See, The Lord Ascends In Triumph
hymns.music: 'Rex Gloriae' Henry Thomas Smart, 1868.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
See, the Lord ascends in triumph;
see the King in royal state,
Riding on the clouds, His chariot,
To His heav'nly palace gate.
Hark! the choirs of angel voices
Joyful alleluias sing,
And the portals high are lifted
To receive their heav'nly King.
Holy Ghost, Illuminator,
shed Thy beams upon our eyes,
Help us to look up with Stephen,
and to see beyond the skies,
Where the Son of Man in glory
Standing is at God's right hand,
Beck'ning on His martyr army,
succoring His faithful band.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
Who is this that comes in glory,
with the trump of jubilee?
Lord of battles, God of armies,
He has gained the victory.
He Who on the cross did suffer,
He who from the grave arose,
He has vanquished sin and Satan,
He by death has spoiled His foes.
See Him, Who is gone before us,
Heav'nly mansions to prepare,
See Him, who is ever pleading
For us with prevailing prayer,
See Him, who with sound of trumpet,
and with His angelic train,
Summoning the world to judgment,
on the clouds will come again.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
While He lifts His hands in blessing,
He is parted from His friends
While their eager eyes behold Him,
He upon the cloud ascends;
He Who walked with God and pleased Him,
preaching truth and doom to come,
He, our Enoch, is translated
to His everlasting home.
Raise us up from earth to Heaven,
give us wings of faith and love,
Gales of holy aspirations
wafting us to realms above;
That, with hearts and minds uplifted,
we with Christ our Lord may dwell,
Where He sits enthroned in glory
in His heav'nly Citadel.

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
Now our heav'nly Aaron enters,
with His blood, within the veil;
Joshua now is come to Canaan,
and the kings before Him quail;
Now He plants the tribes of Israel
in their promised resting place;
Now our great Elijah offers
double portion of His grace.
So at last, when He appeareth,
we from out our graves may spring,
With our youth renewed like eagles,
flocking round our Heav'nly King.
Caught up on the clouds of Heaven,
and may meet Him in the air,
Rise to realms where He is reigning,
and may reign for ever there.

parts.label: Verse 5

hymns.title: Silent Night
hymns.words: Josef Mohr, 1818. stanzas 1,3 Translated by John Freeman Young, 1863.
hymns.music: 'Stille Nacht' Franz Xaver Gruber, 1818.  Setting: "Concordia Kinderchöre", 1908.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
Silent night, holy night,
All is calm, all is bright
Round yon virgin mother and Child.
Holy Infant, so tender and mild,
Sleep in heavenly peace,
Sleep in heavenly peace.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
Silent night, holy night,
Shepherds quake at the sight;
Glories stream from heaven afar,
Heavenly hosts sing Alleluia!
Christ the Savior is born,
Christ the Savior is born!

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
Silent night, holy night,
Son of God, love's pure light;
Radiant beams from Thy holy face
With the dawn of redeeming grace,
Jesus, Lord, at Thy birth,
Jesus, Lord, at Thy birth.

parts.label: Verse 4

hymns.title: Sing, O Sing, This Blessed Morn
hymns.music: 'Nativity' William Henry Monk, 1865.
topics: Adam (first/second - see also Guidance, Invitation [ours to God], Repentance) [4]

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
Sing, O sing, this blessed morn,
Unto us a
Child is born,
Unto us a Son is giv'n, God
Himself comes down from
Heav'n.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
Jesus Christ, the King of kings,
Maker of all worldly things,
Now descends from
Heav'n to Earth,
To re-store us by His birth;

parts.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
God with us, Emmanuel,
Deigns for ever now to dwell; He on
Adam's fallen race
Sheds the fullness of His
Grace;

parts.label: Verse 5
Verse 6
parts.lyrics:
God comes down that man may rise, Lifted far above the skies
He is Son of Man, that we Sons of God in Him may be;

parts.label: Verse 7
parts.lyrics:
Human flesh is now become Christ's abode, the Godhead's home;
Royal Palace, sacred shrine For the Majesty Divine;

parts.label: Verse 8
parts.lyrics:
Now we rise, from prison free; On we march to victory,
Joyful banners are unfurled; 'Tis the Birthday of the World;

parts.label: Verse 9
parts.lyrics:
Now behold the rising Sun Hath His glorious race begun;
Now the Bridegroom from above Weds the Bride, with heavenly love;

parts.label: Verse 10
parts.lyrics:
O renew us, Lord, we pray, With Thy Spirit day by day;
That we ever one may be With the Father, and with Thee;

parts.label: Verse 11
Refrain
parts.lyrics: Sing, O sing, this blessed morn, Jesus Christ today is born.

hymns.title: Songs of Thankfulness and Praise
hymns.music: 'St. George`s Windsor', George Job Elvey, 1858. Setting: "The Anglican Hymn Book", 1871.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
Songs of thankfulness and praise,
Jesus, Lord, to Thee we raise,
Manifested by the star
To the sages from afar;
Branch of royal David's stem
In Thy birth at Bethlehem;
Anthems be to Thee addressed,
God in man made manifest.

parts.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
Sun and moon shall darkened be,
Stars shall fall, the heav'ns shall flee,
Christ will then like lightning shine,
All will see His glorious sign:
All will then the trumpet hear;
All will see the Judge appear;
Thou by all wilt be confessed,
God in man made manifest.

parts.label: Verse 5

hymns.title: Souls of Men! Why Will Ye Scatter
hymns.music: 'In Babilone' traditional Dutch found in "Oude en Nieuwe Hollantse Boerenlities en Contradansen", 1710.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
Souls of men! why will ye scatter
Like a crowd of frightened sheep?
Foolish hearts! why will ye wander
From a love so true and deep?
Was there ever kinder shepherd
Half so gentle, half so sweet,
As the Savior who would have us
Come and gather round His feet?

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
It is God: His love looks mighty,
But is mighti'r than it seems;
'Tis our Father: and His fondness
Goes far out beyond our dreams.
There's a wideness in God's mercy,
Like the wideness of the sea;
There's a kindness in His justice,
Which is more than liberty.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
There is no place where earth's sorrows
Are more felt than up in Heav'n;
There is no place where earth's failings
Have such wondrous judgment giv'n.
There is welcome for the sinner,
Grace poured out as in a flood
There is mercy with the Savior;
There is healing in His blood.

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
There is grace enough for thousands
Of new worlds as great as this;
There is room for fresh creations
In that upper home of bliss.
For the love of God is broader
Than the measure of man's mind;
And the heart of the Eternal
Is most wonderfully kind.

parts.label: Verse 5

hymns.title: Stricken, Smitten, and Afflicted
hymns.tune: O Mein Jesu, Ich Muss Sterben
hymns.music: 'O Mein Jesu, Ich Muss Sterben' or 'Wo Ist Jesus, Mein Verlangen'  from Geistliches Volkslied, 1850.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
Stricken, smitten, and afflicted,
See Him dying on the tree!
'Tis the Christ by man rejected;
Yes, my soul, 'tis He, 'tis He!
'Tis the long expected prophet,
David's Son, yet David's Lord;
Proofs I see sufficient of it:
'Tis a true and faithful Word.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
Tell me, ye who hear Him groaning,
Was there ever grief like His?
Friends through fear His cause disowning,
Foes insulting his distress:
Many hands were raised to wound Him,
None would interpose to save;
But the deepest stroke that pierced Him
Was the stroke that Justice gave.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
Ye who think of sin but lightly,
Nor suppose the evil great,
Here may view its nature rightly,
Here its guilt may estimate.
Mark the Sacrifice appointed!
See Who bears the awful load!
'Tis the Word, the Lord's Anointed,
Son of Man, and Son of God.

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
Here we have a firm foundation,
Here the refuge of the lost.
Christ the Rock of our salvation,
Christ the Name of which we boast.
Lamb of God for sinners wounded!
Sacrifice to cancel guilt!
None shall ever be confounded
Who on Him their hope have built.

hymns.title: Take My Life And Let It Be
hymns.music: 'Mozart' Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart (1756-1791).
topics: Submission (see also Following Jesus, God - Providence of, Trust)

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
Take my life, and let it be
consecrated, Lord, to Thee.
Take my moments and my days;
let them flow in ceaseless praise.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
Take my hands, and let them move
at the impulse of Thy love.
Take my feet, and let them be
swift and beautiful for Thee.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
Take my voice, and let me sing
always, only, for my King.
Take my lips, and let them be
filled with messages from Thee.

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
Take my silver and my gold;
not a mite would I withhold.
Take my intellect, and use
every pow'r as Thou shalt choose.

parts.label: Verse 5
Verse 6
parts.lyrics:
Take my love, my Lord, I pour at Thy feet its treasure store.
Take myself, and I will be ever, only, all for Thee.

hymns.title: Take Thou My Hand and Lead Me
hymns.music: 'So Nimm Denn Meine Hände' Friedrich Silcher, 1842.  Setting: Donna Snell, circa 1975.
topics: Children (see also God's Children - the Faithful) [2]

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
Take Thou my hand, and lead me o'er life's rough way,
with Heav'nly Manna feed me from day to day.
Alone my footsteps falter and straggle wide,
Lord who my life canst alter be Thou my guide.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
Take Thou my heart and hide it in folds of grace
Though pain or woe betide it to know Thy face
Draw, Lord, of Thy good pleasure Thy child to Thee,
And grant me faith's full measure though naught I see.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
Though oft I think Thou hidest Thy wondrous might,
Still to my goal Thou guidest me through dark night,
Take, then, my hands and lead me till life is o'er,
With heav'nly manna feed me forevermore.

hymns.title: That Men a godly Life Might Live
hymns.tune: Dies sind die heil`gen zehu Gebot
hymns.words: Martin Luther, 1524.  Translated by Richard Massie, 1854, alt.
hymns.music: 'Dies sind die heil`gen zehu Gebot' or 'In Gottes Namen fahren wir' circa
topics: Submission (see also Following Jesus, God - Providence of, Trust)

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
That man a godly life might live,
God did these ten commandments give
By His true servant Moses, high
Upon the mount Sinai.
Have mercy, Lord.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
I am thy God and Lord alone,
No other God besides Me own;
On My great mercy venture thee,
With all thy heart love thou Me.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
By idle word and speech profane
Take not My holy Name in vain;
And praise not aught as good and true
But what God doth say and do.

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
Hallow the day which God hath blest,
That thou and all thy house may rest;
Keep hand and heart from labor free,
That God may so work in thee.

parts.label: Verse 5
parts.lyrics:
Give to thy parents honor due,
Be dutiful and loving too;
And help them when their strength decays
So shalt thou have length of days.

hymns.title: The Advent of Our God
hymns.words: Charles Coffin, 1736.  translated by John Chandler, 1837, alt.
hymns.music: 'St. Thomas' Aaron Williams, 1770.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
The advent of our God
Shall be our theme for prayer
Come, let us meet him on the road
And place for Him prepare.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
The everlasting Son
Incarnate stoops to be,
Himself the servant's form puts on
To set His people free.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
Come, Zion's daughter, rise
To meet your lowly King,
Nor let your faithless heart despise
The peace He comes to bring.

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
As judge, on clouds of light,
He soon will come again
And all His scattered saints unite
With Him on high to reign.

parts.label: Verse 5
parts.lyrics:
Before the dawning day
Let sin be put to flight;
No longer let the law hold sway,
But walk in freedom's light.

parts.label: Verse 6
parts.lyrics:
All glory to the Son
Who comes to set us free,
With Father, Spirit, ever One,
Through all eternity.

hymns.title: The Bridegroom Soon Will Call Us
hymns.words: Johann Walther, 1552. Translated by Matthias Loy, 1880.
hymns.music: 'Act Gott Vom Himmelreiche' or 'Ich will ein Neues Singen' or 'Praetorius 7' from Musae Sionae

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
The Bridegroom soon will call us,
Come, all ye wedding guests!
May not His voice appall us,
While slumber binds our breasts;
May all our lamps be burning,
And oil be found in store,
That we, with Him returning,
May open find the door.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
There shall we see delighted
Our dear Redeemer's face,
Who leads our souls benighted
To glory by His grace;
The patriarchs shall meet us,
The prophets' holy band,
Apostles, martyrs, greet us
In that celestial land.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
They will not blush to own us
As brothers, sisters dear,
Love ever will be shown us
When we with them appear;
We all shall come before Him,
Who for us Man became,
As Lord and God adore Him,
And ever bless His Name.

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
Our Father, rich in blessing,
Will give us crowns of gold
And, to His bosom pressing,
Impart a bliss untold,
Will welcome with embraces
Of never ending love,
And deck us with His graces
In blissful realms above.

parts.label: Verse 5
parts.lyrics:
In yonder home shall never
Be silent music's voice;
With hearts and lips forever
We shall in God rejoice;
The angels shall adore Him,
All saints shall sing His praise,
And bring with joy before Him
Their sweetest heav'nly lays.

hymns.title: The Church's One Foundation
hymns.music: 'Aurelia' Samuel Sebastian Wesley, 1864.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
The Church's one foundation
Is Jesus Christ her Lord,
She is His new creation
By water and the Word.
From heav'n He came and sought her
To be His holy bride;
With His own blood He bought her
And for her life He died.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
She is from every nation,
Yet one o'er all the earth;
Her charter of salvation,
One Lord, one faith, one birth;
One holy Name she blesses,
Partakes one holy food,
And to one hope she presses,
With every grace endued.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
The Church shall never perish!
Her dear Lord to defend,
To guide, sustain, and cherish,
Is with her to the end:
Though there be those who hate her,
And false sons in her pale,
Against or foe or traitor
She ever shall prevail.

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
Though with a scornful wonder
Men see her sore oppressed,
By schisms rent asunder,
By heresies distressed:
Yet saints their watch are keeping,
Their cry goes up, 'How long?'
And soon the night of weeping
Shall be the morn of song!

parts.label: Verse 5
parts.lyrics:
'Mid toil and tribulation,
And tumult of her war,
She waits the consummation
Of peace forevermore;
Till, with the vision glorious,
Her longing eyes are blest,
And the great Church victorious
Shall be the Church at rest.

parts.label: Verse 6
parts.lyrics:
Yet she on earth hath union
With God the Three in One,
And mystic sweet communion
With those whose rest is won,
With all her sons and daughters
Who, by the Master's hand
Led through the deathly waters,
Repose in Eden land.

parts.label: Verse 7
parts.lyrics:
O happy ones and holy!
Lord, give us grace that we
Like them, the meek and lowly,
On high may dwell with Thee:
There, past the border mountains,
Where in sweet vales the Bride
With Thee by living fountains
Forever shall abide!

hymns.title: The Comforter Has Come
hymns.music: 'The Comforter Has Come' William J. Kirkpatrick, 1890.  Setting: "Pentecostal Hymns, No. 2", 1898.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
O spread the tidings 'round, wherever man is found,
Wherever human hearts and human woes abound;
Let ev'ry Christian tongue proclaim the joyful sound:
The Comforter has come!

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
The long, long night is past, the morning breaks at last,
And hush'd the dreadful wail and fury of the blast,
As o'er the golden hills the day advances fast!
The Comforter has come!

parts.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
O boundless love divine! how shall this tongue of mine
To wond'ring mortals tell the matchless grace divine;
That I, a child of hell, should in His image shine!
The Comforter has come!

parts.label: Verse 5
parts.lyrics:
Sing, till the echoes fly above the vaulted sky,
And all the saints above to all below reply,
In strains of endless love the song that ne'er will die:
The Comforter has come!

parts.label: Refrain
parts.lyrics:
The Comforter has come,
The Comforter has come!
The Holy Ghost from heav'n,
The Father's promise giv'n; O spread the tidings 'round,
Wherever man is found:
The Comforter has come!

hymns.title: The Day is Surely Drawing Near
hymns.tune: Es ist Gewisslich an der Zeit
hymns.words: Bartholomäus Ringwaldt, 1565.  Translated by Phillip A. Peter, 1872, alt.
hymns.music: 'Es ist Gewisslich an der Zeit' from Klug's Geistliche Lieder, Wittenberg, 1533.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
The day is surely drawing near,
When God's Son, the Anointed,
Shall with great majesty appear,
As Judge of all appointed.
All mirth and laughter then shall cease
When flames on flames will still increase,
As Scripture truly teacheth.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
A trumpet loud shall then resound,
And all the earth be shaken;
Then all who in their graves are found
Shall from their sleep awaken.
But all that live shall in that hour,
By the Almighty's boundless pow'r
Be changed at His commanding.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
A book is opened then to all,
A record truly telling
What each hath done, both great and small,
When he on earth was dwelling;
And every heart be clearly seen,
And all be known as they have been,
In thoughts and words and actions.

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
Then woe to those who scorned the Lord,
And sought but carnal pleasures,
Who here despised His precious Word,
And loved their earthly treasures!
With shame and trembling they will stand,
And at the Judge's stern command
To Satan be delivered.

parts.label: Verse 5
parts.lyrics:
O Jesus, who my debt didst pay
And for my sin wast smitten
Within the Book of Life, oh, may
My name be also written!
I will not doubt; I trust in Thee,
From Satan Thou hast made me free
And from all condemnation.

hymns.title: The First Noel
hymns.words: Traditional English carol, possibly dating from as early as the 13th Century.
hymns.music: 'The First Noel' Traditional English carol, possibly dating from as early as the 13th Century.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
The first Noel the angel did say
Was to certain poor shepherds in fields as they lay;
In fields where they lay tending their sheep,
On a cold winter's night that was so deep.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
They lookèd up and saw a star
Shining in the east, beyond them far;
And to the earth it gave great light,
And so it continued both day and night.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
And by the light of that same star
Three Wise Men came from country far;
To seek for a King was their intent,
And to follow the star wherever it went.

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
This star drew nigh to the northwest,
Over Bethlehem it took its rest;
And there it did both stop and stay,
Right over the place where Jesus lay.

parts.label: Verse 5
parts.lyrics:
Then did they know assuredly
Within that house the King did lie;
One entered it them for to see,
And found the
Babe in poverty.

parts.label: Refrain
parts.lyrics:
Noel, Noel, Noel,
Noel, Born is the King of Israel.

hymns.title: The Galilean Fishers Toil
hymns.music: 'Old 137th' or 'Norwich' from Day's Psalter, 1563.  Setting: "The Holy Year", 1865.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
The Galilean fishers toil
all night, and nothing take;
But Jesus comes,- a wondrous spoil
is lifted from the lake.
Lord, when our labors are in vain
and vain the help of men,
When fruitless is our care and pain,
Come blessed Jesus then!

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
The night is dark, the surges fill
the bark, the wild winds roar;
But Jesus comes and all is still,-
the ship is at the shore.
O Lord, when storms around us howl,
and all is dark and drear,
In all the tempests of the soul,
O blessed Jesus hear.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
A frail one, thrice denying Thee
saw mercy in Thine eyes,
The penitent upon the tree
was borne to Paradise.
In hours of sin and deep distress
o show us, Lord, Thy Face,
In penitential loneliness,
O give us Jesus grace!

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
The faithful few retire in fear
to their closed upper room;
But suddenly with joyful cheer
they see their Master come.
Lord come to us, unloose our bands
and bid our terrors cease,
Lift over us Thy blessed hands,
Speak, holy Jesus Peace!

parts.label: Verse 5
parts.lyrics:
In days, when faith will scarce be found,
and wolves be in the fold,
When sin and sorrow will abound
and charity wax cold,
Then hear Thy saints, who to Thee pray
to bring them to their home,
Hear when the Bride and Spirit say,
"Come, Blessed Jesus, Come!"

hymns.title: The God of Abraham Praise
hymns.words: Daniel ben Judah, circa 1400. Paraphrased by Thomas Olivers, circa 1765.
hymns.music: 'Yigdal' or 'Leoni' Traditional Hebrew. Setting: Meyer Lyon, 1780.

parts.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
The God of Abr'ham praise,
Whose all sufficient grace
Shall guide me all my happy days, in all my ways.
He calls a worm His friend,
He calls Himself my God!
And He shall save me to the end, thro' Jesus' blood.

parts.label: Verse 4
Verse 5
parts.lyrics:
Tho' nature's strength decay,
and earth and hell withstand,
To Canaan's bounds I urge my way, at His command.
The wat'ry deep I pass,
with Jesus in my view;
And thro' the howling wilderness my way pursue.

hymns.title: The Gospel Shows The Father's Grace
hymns.tune: Herr Jesu Christ, Dict Zu Uns Wend
hymns.music: 'Herr Jesu Christ, Dict Zu Uns Wend' from Cantionale Germanicum, Dresden, 1628.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
The Gospel shows the Father's grace,
Who sent his Son to save our race,
Proclaims how Jesus lived and died
That man might thus be justified.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
It sets the Lamb before our eyes,
Who made th'atoning sacrifice,
And calls the souls with guilt oppressed
To come and find eternal rest.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
It brings the Savior's righteousness
Our souls to robe in royal dress;
From all our guilt it brings release
And gives the troubled conscience peace.

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
It is the pow'r of God to save
From sin and Satan and the grave;
It works the faith, which firmly clings
To all the treasures which it brings.

parts.label: Verse 5
parts.lyrics:
It bears to all the tidings glad
And bids their hearts no more be sad;
The heavy laden souls it cheers
And banishes their guilty fears.

parts.label: Verse 6
parts.lyrics:
May we in faith its tidings learn
Nor thanklessly its blessings spurn;
May we in faith its truth confess
And praise the Lord our Righteousness!

hymns.title: The King Shall Come
hymns.words: Unknown author. Translated by John Brownlie, 1907.
hymns.music: 'Consolation' or 'Morning Song' John Wyeth, 1813.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
The King shall come when morning dawns,
And light triumphant breaks;
When beauty gilds the eastern hills,
And life to joy awakes.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
Not as of old a little child
To bear, and fight, and die,
But crowned with glory like the sun
That lights the morning sky.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
O brighter than the rising morn
When He, victorious, rose,
And left the lonesome place of death,
Despite the rage of foes.

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
O brighter than that glorious morn
Shall this fair morning be,
When Christ, our King, in beauty comes,
And we His face shall see.

parts.label: Verse 5
parts.lyrics:
The King shall come when morning dawns,
And earth's dark night is past;
O haste the rising of that morn,
The day that aye shall last.

parts.label: Verse 6
parts.lyrics:
And let the endless bliss begin,
By weary saints foretold,
When right shall triumph over wrong,
And truth shall be extolled.

parts.label: Verse 7
parts.lyrics:
The King shall come when morning dawns,
And light and beauty brings:
Hail, Christ the Lord! Thy people pray,
Come quickly, King of kings.

hymns.title: The Law Of God Is Good And Wise
hymns.tune: Erhalt Uns, Herr, bei deinem Wort
hymns.music: 'Erhalt Uns, Herr, bei deinem Wort' from Klug's Geistliche Lieder, 1543.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
The law of God is good and wise,
And sets His will before our eyes,
Shows us the way of righteousness,
And dooms to death when we transgress.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
Its light of holiness imparts
The knowledge of our sinful hearts,
That we may see our lost estate
And seek deliv'rance ere too late.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
To those who help in Christ have found
And would in works of love abound
It shows what deeds are His delight
And should be done as good and right.

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
When men the offered help disdain
And willfully in sin remain,
Its terror in their ear resounds
And keeps their wickedness in bounds.

parts.label: Verse 5
parts.lyrics:
The law is good, but since the fall
Its holiness condemns us all;
It dooms us for our sin to die
And has no pow'r to justify.

hymns.title: The Lily of the Valley
hymns.music: 'Salvation' or 'The Lily of the Valley' William S. Hays, 1881.  Setting: Ira D. Sankey, 1887.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
I've found a friend in Jesus,
He's everything to me,
He's the fairest of ten thousand to my soul;
The Lily of the
Valley, in Him alone I see
All I need to cleanse and make me fully whole.
In sorrow He's my comfort, in trouble
He's my stay; He tells me every care on Him to roll.
He's the Lily

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
He all my grief has taken, and all my sorrows borne;
In temptation He's my strong and mighty tow'r;
I'll all for Him forsake now,
I'll all my idols tear
From my heart for now He keeps me by His pow'r.
Though all the world forsake me, and
Satan tempt me sore,
Through Jesus I shall safely reach the goal.
He's the Lily

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
He'll never, never leave me, nor yet forsake me here,
So I live by faith and do His blessed will;
A wall of fire about me,
I've nothing now to fear,
With His manna He my hungry soul shall fill.
When crown'd at last in glory,
I'll see His blessed face,
Where rivers of delight shall ever roll.
He's the Lily

parts.label: Refrain
parts.lyrics:
of the Valley, the
Bright and Morning
Star, He's the fairest of ten thousand to my soul.

hymns.title: The Lord's My Shepherd
hymns.words: Psalm 23 from the Scottish Psalter, 1650 alt. by James Leith Macbeth Bain, 1915.
hymns.music: 'Marosa' or 'Brother James` Air' James Leith Macbeth Bain, 1915, alt.
topics: God's Children - the Faithful (see also Saints, People of the World)

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
The Lord's my shepherd I'll not want,
He makes me down to lie
In pastures green He leadeth me
The quiet waters by.
He leadeth me, He leadeth me,
The quiet waters by,
In pastures green He leadeth me
The quiet waters by.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
My soul He doth restore again,
And me to walk doth make.
Within the paths of blessedness,
E'en for His Own Name's sake;
His Own Name's sake, His Own Name's sake,
E'en for His Own Name's sake;
Within the paths of blessedness,
E'en for His Own Name's sake.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
Yea, though I walk in death's dark vale,
Yet will I fear no ill,
For Thou art with me, and Thy rod
And staff me comfort still;
I'll fear no ill, I'll fear no ill,
Yet will I fear no ill,
For Thou art with me, and Thy rod
And staff me comfort still.

parts.label: Verse 4
Verse 5
parts.lyrics:
Goodness and mercy all my days
Will surely follow me:
And in my Father's heart always
My dwelling place shall be;
My dwelling place, My dwelling place,
My dwelling place shall be,
And in my Father's heart always
My dwelling place shall be.

hymns.title: The Love of God
hymns.music: 'The Love of God' Frederick Martin Lehman, 1917.  Setting: Claudia Lehman Mays, 1917.
topics: Children (see also God's Children - the Faithful) [1]

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
The love of God is greater far
Than tongue or pen can ever tell,
It goes beyond the highest star,
And reaches to the lowest hell;
The guilty pair, bowed down with care, God gave His Son to win; His erring child, He reconciled,
And pardoned from his sin.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
When hoary time shall pass away,
And earthly thrones and kingdoms fall;
When men who here refuse to pray,
On rocks and hills and mountains call; God's love, so sure, shall still endure,
All measureless and strong;
Redeeming grace to
Adam's race- The saints' and angels' song.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
Could we with ink the ocean fill,
And were the skies of parchment made,
Were every stalk on earth a quill
And every man a scribe by trade;
To write the love of God above
Would drain the ocean dry;
Nor could the scroll contain the whole,
Tho' stretched from sky to sky.

parts.label: Refrain
parts.lyrics:
Oh love of God, how rich and pure!
How measureless and strong!
It shall forevermore endure,
The saints' and angels' song.

hymns.title: The Mouth of Fools Doth God Confess
hymns.words: Martin Luther, 1524.  Translated by Richard Massie, 1854, alt.
hymns.music: 'Es spricht der Unweisen Mund' from Walter's Geistliche Gesangbüchlein, 1524.  Setting: Michael Praetorius, 1610.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
The mouth of fools doth God confess,
But while their lips draw nigh Him,
Their heart is full of wickedness,
And all their deeds deny Him.
Corrupt are they, and every one
Abominable works hath done;
There is not one welldoer.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
The Lord looked down from his high tow'r
On all mankind below Him,
To see if any owned His pow'r,
And truly sought to know Him;
Who all their understanding bent
To search His holy Word, intent
To do his will in earnest.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
But none there was who walked with God,
For all aside had slidden,
Delusive paths of folly trod,
And followed lusts forbidden;
Not one there was who practiced good,
And yet they deemed, in haughty mood,
Their deeds must surely please Him.

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
How long, by folly blindly led,
Will ye oppress the needy,
And eat my people up like bread?
So fierce are ye, and greedy!
In God they put no trust at all,
Nor will on Him in trouble call,
But be their own providers.

parts.label: Verse 5
parts.lyrics:
Therefore their heart is never still,
A falling leaf dismays them;
God is with him who doth His will,
Who trusts him and obeys Him;
But ye the poor man's hope despise,
And laugh at him, e'en when he cries,
That God is his sure comfort.

parts.label: Verse 6
parts.lyrics:
Who shall to Israel's outcast race From Zion bring salvation?
God will himself at length show grace, And loose the captive nation;
That will he do by Christ their King; Let Jacob then be
glad and sing, And Israel be joyful.

hymns.title: The Old Rugged Cross
hymns.music: 'The Old Rugged Cross' George Bennard, 1913.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
On a hill far away stood an old rugged cross,
The emblem of suff'ring and shame;
And I love that old cross where the dearest and best
For a world of lost sinners was slain.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
O that old rugged cross, so despised by the world,
Has a wondrous attraction for me;
For the dear Lamb of God left His glory above
To bear it to dark
Calvary.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
In that old rugged cross, stained with blood so divine,
A wondrous beauty I see,
For 'twas on that old cross Jesus suffered and died,
To pardon and sanctify me.

parts.label: Verse 4
Refrain
parts.lyrics:
So I'll cherish the old rugged cross,
Till my trophies at last I lay down; I will cling to the old rugged cross,
And exchange it some day for a crown.

hymns.title: The People That in Darkness Sat
hymns.music: 'Lobt Gott, ihr Christen Allzugleich' Nikolaus Hermann, 1554.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
The people that in darkness sat
A glorious light have seen;
The light has shined on them who long
In shades of death have been.
In shades of death have been.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
To hail Thee, Sun of Righteousness,
The gath'ring nations come;
They joy as when the reapers bear
Their harvest treasures home.
Their harvest treasures home.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
For Thou their burden dost remove
And break the tyrant's rod
As in the day when Midian fell
Before the sword of God.
Before the sword of God.

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
To us a Child of hope is born,
To us a Son is giv'n,
And on His shoulder ever rests
All pow'r in earth and heav'n.
All pow'r in earth and heav'n.

parts.label: Verse 5
parts.lyrics:
His name shall be the Prince of Peace,
The Everlasting Lord,
The Wonderful, the Counselor.
The God by all adored.
The God by all adored.

parts.label: Verse 6
parts.lyrics:
His righteous government and power
Shall over all extend;
On judgment and on justice based,
His reign shall have no end.

parts.label: Verse 7
parts.lyrics:
Lord Jesus, reign in us, we pray,
And make us Thine alone,
Who with the Father ever art
And Holy Spirit, one.

hymns.title: The Star Proclaims the King is Here
hymns.words: Coelius Sedulius, c. 450. German version by M. Luther, 1543.  English translation by John Mason Neale, 1852.
hymns.music: 'Wo Gott Zum Haus' from Klug's Geistliche Lieder, Wittenberg, 1533.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
The star proclaims the King is here;
But, Herod, why this senseless fear?
He takes no realms of earth away
Who gives the realms of heav'nly day.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
The wiser Magi see from far
And follow on His guiding star;
And led by light, to light they press
And by their gifts their God confess.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
Within the Jordan's crystal flood
In meekness stands the Lamb of God
And, sinless, sanctifies the wave,
Mankind from sin to cleanse and save.

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
At Cana first His pow'r is shown;
His might the blushing waters own
And, changing as He speaks the word,
Flow wine, obedient to their Lord.

parts.label: Verse 5
parts.lyrics:
All glory, Jesus, be to Thee
For this Thy glad epiphany;
Whom with the Father we adore
And Holy Ghost forevermore.

hymns.title: The Strife Is O'er, The Battle Done
hymns.words: from Symphonia Sirenum Selectarum, Köln, 1695; translated by Francis Pott, 1861.
hymns.music: 'Victory' or  'Palestrina' Giovanni P. da Palestrina, 1591.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
The strife is o'er, the battle done;
The triumph of the Lord is won; O
Let the song of praise be sung:
Alleluia!

parts.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
On that third morn He rose again
In glorious majesty to reign; O let us swell the joyful strain.
Alleluia!

parts.label: Verse 4
Verse 5
parts.lyrics:
Lord, by the stripes which wounded Thee,
From death's dread sting Thy servants free,
That we may live, and sing to Thee.
Alleluia!

parts.label: Refrain
parts.lyrics:
Alleluia, Alleluia, Alleluia.
Alleluia, Alleluia, Alleluia.

hymns.title: The Winds and Billows Loudly Roar
hymns.music: 'Consolation' or 'Morning Song' John Wyeth, 1813.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
The winds and billows loudly roar
We flounder in the deep
Our bark is frail, far off the shore,
And Jesus is asleep.

parts.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
His head is pillow'd on the stern,
As Man He is asleep;
As God He all things does discern,
And endless vigils keep.

parts.label: Verse 4
Verse 5
parts.lyrics:
O ye, who in the Church's Bark
O'er life's rough ocean sail,
When all around is drear and dark,
and human efforts fail,

parts.label: Verse 6
parts.lyrics:
Touch not, with rude, irreverent hands,
And coward faithlessness,
Him, who the winds and waves commands;
But wait in quietness.

parts.label: Verse 7
parts.lyrics:
O never, never when distressed,
To doubtful means resort;
Christ's Bark, when on the billow's crest,
Is safe as in the port.

hymns.title: There's a Great Day Coming
hymns.music: 'Theres a Great Day Coming' Will L. Thompson, 1886.  Setting: "Alexander's Hymns No. 3", 1915.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
There's a great day coming,
A great day coming,
There's a great day coming by and by;
When the saints and the sinners shall be parted right and left,

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
There's a bright day coming,
A bright day coming,
There's a bright day coming by and by;
But its brightness shall only come to them that love the Lord,

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
There's a sad day coming,
A sad day coming,
There's a sad day coming by and by;
When the sinner shall hear his doom,
"Depart, I know ye not,"

parts.label: Refrain
parts.lyrics:
Are you ready for that day to come?
Are you ready?
Are you ready?
Are you ready for the judgment day?
Are you ready?
Are you ready?
For the judgment day?

hymns.title: Thine Arm, O Lord, in Days of Old

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
Thine arm, O Lord, in days of old,
was strong to heal and save;
It triumphed o'er disease and death,
o'er darkness and the grave.
To Thee they went, the blind, the dumb,
the palsied and the lame,
The leper with his tainted life,
the sick with fevered frame.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
And lo! Thy touch brought life and health,
gave speech, and strength and sight;
And youth renewed and fear relieved
owned Thee, the Lord of light;
And now, O Lord, be near to bless,
Almighty as of yore,
In crowded street, by restless couch,
as by Gennesaret's shore.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
Be Thou our great Deliverer still,
Thou Lord of life and death;
Restore and quicken, soothe and bless,
with Thine almighty breath.
To hands that work and eyes that see,
give wisdom's heavenly lore,
That whole and sick, and weak and strong,
may praise Thee evermore.

hymns.title: Thou, Who at Thy First Eucharist
hymns.music: 'Unde Et Memores' William Henry Monk, 1875.
topics: Submission (see also Following Jesus, God - Providence of, Trust)

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
Thou, who at Thy first Eucharist didst pray
That all Thy Church might be forever one,
Grant us at ev'ry Eucharist to say
With longing heart and soul, "Thy will be done."
O may we all one bread, one body be,
Through this blest sacrament of unity.

parts.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
So, Lord, at length when sacraments shall cease,
May we be one with all Thy Church above,
One with Thy saints in one unbroken peace,
One with Thy saints in one unbounded love;
More blessèd still, in peace and love to be
One with the Trinity in unity.

hymns.title: Though in the Midst of Life We Be
hymns.words: v.1 Medieval sequence, vs 2,3 Martin Luther, 1524.  Translated by Richard Massie, 1854, alt.
hymns.music: 'Mitten wir im Leben Sind' Medieval sequence altered by Martin Luther.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
Though in midst of life we be,
Snares of death surround us;
Where shall we for succor flee,
Lest our foes confound us?
To Thee alone, our Savior.
We mourn our grievous sin which hath
Stirr'd the fire of Thy fierce wrath. Savior! Thou eternal God!
Save us, Lord, from sinking
In the deep and bitter flood.
Kyrie eleison.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
Whilst in midst of death we be,
Hell's grim jaws o'ertake us; Who from such distress will free. Who secure will make us? Thou only, Lord, canst do it!
It moves Thy tender heart to see
Our great sin and misery. Savior! Thou eternal God!
Let not hell dismay us
With its deep and burning flood.
Kyrie eleison.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
Into hell's fierce agony
Sin doth headlong drive us:
Where shall we for succor flee, Who, O, who will hide us? Thou only, blessed Saviour. Thy precious blood was shed to win
Peace and pardon for our sin. Savior!
Let us not, we pray,
From the true faith's comfort
Fall in our last need away.
Kyrie eleison.

parts.label: Refrain
parts.lyrics: Holy and gracious God! Holy and mighty God! Holy and all- merciful

hymns.title: Through the Night of Doubt and Sorrow
hymns.words: Bernhardt S. Ingemann, 1826. Translated by Sabine Baring-Gould, 1867.
hymns.music: 'Rex Gloriae' Henry Thomas Smart, 1868.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
Through the night of doubt and sorrow
Onward goes the pilgrim band,
Singing songs of expectation,
Marching to the Promised Land.
Clear before us through the darkness
Gleams and burns the guiding light:
Brother clasps the hand of brother,
Stepping fearless through the night.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
One the light of God's own presence,
O'er His ransomed people shed,
Chasing far the gloom and terror,
Bright'ning all the path we tread:
One the object of our journey,
One the faith which never tires,
One the earnest looking forward,
One the hope our God inspires.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
One the strain that lips of thousands
Lift as from the heart of one;
One the conflict, one the peril
One the march in God begun:
One the gladness of rejoicing
On the far eternal shore,
Where the One Almighty Father
Reigns in love for evermore.

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
Onward, therefore, pilgrim brothers,
Onward, with the cross our aid!
Bear its shame, and fight its battle,
Till we rest beneath its shade.
Soon shall come the great awaking,
Soon the rending of the tomb;
Then the scatt'ring of all shadows,
And the end of toil and gloom.

hymns.title: Tis Good, Lord, To Be Here
hymns.music: 'Potsdam' adapted from Johann Sebastian Bach, 1750, by John Goss, 1854. Setting: John Goss, 1854.

parts.label: Verse 1
parts.lyrics:
'Tis good, Lord, to be here,
Thy glory fills the night;
Thy face and garments, like the sun,
Shine with unborrowed light.

parts.label: Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
'Tis good, Lord, to be here,
Thy beauty to behold
Where Moses and Elijah stand,
Thy messengers of old.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
Fulfiller of the past,
Promise of things to be,
We hail Thy body glorified
And our redemption see.

parts.label: Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
Before we taste of death,
We see Thy Kingdom come;
We fain would hold the vision bright
And make this hill our home.

parts.label: Verse 5
parts.lyrics:
'Tis good, Lord, to be here.
Yet we may not remain;
But since Thou bidst us leave the mount,
Come with us to the plain.

hymns.title: To Avert From Men God's Wrath
hymns.words: Latin c. 1400, sometimes attr. John Hus.  Translated Christian Ignatius Latrobe, 1789.
hymns.music: 'Gethsemane' or 'Petra' Richard Redhead, 1853.

parts.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
That we never should forget
This great Love on us bestowed,
He gave us His flesh to eat,
and to drink His precious blood;
All who sick and needy are
May receive in Him a share.

parts.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
parts.lyrics:
He who in self- righteousness
Fixes any hope or stay,
Has not on a wedding dress,
And with shame is sent away;
To the hungry, weary heart,
He will food and rest impart.

parts.label: Verse 5
parts.lyrics:
But examine first your case,
Whether you be in the faith;
Do you long for pard'ning grace?
Is your only hope His death?
Then, howe'er your soul's oppressed,
Come, you are a worthy guest.

parts.label: Verse 6

hymns.title: To God Be The Glory
hymns.music: 'To God Be The Glory' William Howard Doane, 1875.

parts.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
parts.lyrics:
O perfect redemption, the purchase of blood,
To every believer the promise of God;
The vilest offender who truly believes,
That moment from Jesus a pardon receives.

parts.label: Verse 3
parts.lyrics:
Great things He has taught us, great things He has done,
And great our rejoicing through Jesus the Son;
But purer, and higher, and greater will be
Our wonder, our transport, when Jesus we see.
